notes.title: Motion — Revision Notes
notes.content:
# Motion — Revision Notes

## Introduction
Motion is the first formal physics chapter of Class 9: you learn to describe *how* things move using distance, displacement, velocity and acceleration, and to read motion graphs. It sets the language for Newton's laws in the next chapter.

## Key Concepts

### Distance vs displacement
Distance is the total path length — a scalar. Displacement is the straight-line shortest separation between start and end points with direction — a vector. On a closed round trip, distance is large but displacement is zero.

### Speed vs velocity
Speed = distance/time (scalar). Velocity = displacement/time (vector). Average velocity for uniform acceleration = (u + v)/2. Instantaneous velocity is what the speedometer shows at a moment.

### Acceleration
Acceleration a = (v − u)/t, unit m/s². Positive when speeding up, negative (retardation) when slowing down. Uniform acceleration means the velocity changes by equal amounts in equal times.

### Three equations of motion (uniform acceleration)
1. v = u + at
2. s = ut + ½at²
3. v² = u² + 2as
Here u = initial velocity, v = final velocity, s = displacement, t = time. Choose the equation that links the three quantities you know with the one you want.

### Graphs
- Distance-time: slope = speed. Straight sloping line = uniform speed; horizontal line = rest; curve = changing speed.
- Velocity-time: slope = acceleration; **area under the curve = displacement**. A horizontal v-t line means uniform velocity.

### Uniform circular motion
An object moving on a circle with constant speed is still accelerating, because its **direction** keeps changing. Velocity is tangential; acceleration points to the centre. Example: a stone whirled on a thread.

## Example
A bus slows from 20 m/s to rest in 5 s uniformly. Find acceleration and distance.
a = (0 − 20)/5 = −4 m/s² (retardation).
s = ut + ½at² = 20×5 + ½(−4)(25) = 100 − 50 = 50 m.
Or v² = u² + 2as → s = (0 − 400)/(2×(−4)) = 50 m ✓

## Quick Revision
- Displacement can be zero even when distance is not.
- Average velocity = (u + v)/2 only for uniform acceleration.
- Slope of s-t graph = speed; slope of v-t graph = acceleration.
- Area under v-t graph = distance travelled.
- Negative acceleration is retardation, not negative motion.
- Uniform circular motion has constant speed but changing velocity.

## Exam Tips
- Draw the v-t graph before solving long numericals; the area method often saves time.
- Always convert units first (km/h → m/s by dividing by 3.6).
- Write the equation number you are using — numericals are step-marked.
- In round-trip questions, compute distance and displacement separately.
- Remember "rest" appears as a horizontal line on BOTH graph types but at s = constant or v = 0 respectively.
keyPoints: Displacement can be zero even when distance is not.
Average velocity = (u + v)/2 only for uniform acceleration.
Slope of s-t graph = speed; slope of v-t graph = acceleration.
Area under v-t graph = distance travelled.
Negative acceleration is retardation, not negative motion.
Uniform circular motion has constant speed but changing velocity.

notes.title: Chemical Reactions and Equations — Revision Notes
notes.content:
# Chemical Reactions and Equations — Revision Notes

## Introduction
This opening chapter trains you to read and write chemical equations correctly and to classify reactions — the skill behind almost every later chemistry chapter. Expect 3-5 marks from this chapter in boards, mostly as equation-based questions.

## Key Concepts

### Writing a balanced equation
A chemical equation must obey the **law of conservation of mass**: atoms of each element must be equal on both sides. Balancing is done by adjusting coefficients (the big numbers), never the subscripts. States are shown as (s), (l), (g), (aq). Conditions like heat are written above the arrow.

### Combination & decomposition
- **Combination**: two or more reactants form one product, e.g. CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ + heat. Quicklime slaking is strongly exothermic.
- **Decomposition**: one reactant breaks into several, needing energy: thermal (heat), electrolytic (electricity, e.g. water → H₂ + O₂), or photolytic (light, e.g. silver chloride greying in sunlight — used in photography).

### Displacement & double displacement
- **Displacement**: a more reactive metal pushes out a less reactive one from its salt solution, e.g. Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu (blue fades to green). The reactivity series decides who wins.
- **Double displacement**: ions swap partners. If an insoluble solid forms, it is a **precipitation reaction**; if heat is released between two solutions, it is a **neutralisation**.

### Redox idea
Oxidation = gain of oxygen / loss of electrons; reduction = loss of oxygen / gain of electrons. In ZnO + C → Zn + CO, carbon is the reducing agent and zinc oxide is reduced. In photosynthesis the reverse pairing happens.

### Exothermic vs endothermic
Exothermic reactions release heat (respiration, burning, slaking of lime). Endothermic reactions absorb heat (decomposition of limestone, photosynthesis). Both are common 1-mark "identify the type" questions.

### Corrosion & rancidity
Corrosion: metal surface is attacked by air/moisture (rust on iron, black coating on silver, green patina on copper). Prevention: painting, oiling, galvanisation, alloying. Rancidity: fats/oils oxidise giving bad smell; prevented by antioxidants, airtight packaging, nitrogen flushing (chip packets).

## Example
Balance: Fe + H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + H₂ (steam).
Balanced form: 3Fe + 4H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + 4H₂. Count: Fe 3=3, H 8=8, O 4=4 ✓ Type: displacement + redox.

## Quick Revision
- Balance by counting atoms element-by-element; smallest whole-number coefficients win.
- Combination: many → one. Decomposition: one → many.
- More reactive metal displaces less reactive metal from its salt.
- Precipitate = insoluble product in double displacement.
- Oxidation and reduction always happen together (redox).
- Silver chloride turns grey in light — photolytic decomposition.
- Rancid chips packets are flushed with nitrogen.

## Exam Tips
- Always write physical states when asked for a "complete" equation — marks are reserved for them.
- Name the type of reaction **and** justify in one line; naming alone often loses half marks.
- For balancing, tally atoms in a small table; it prevents silly slip-ups.
- Learn the reactivity series mnemonic up to copper — displacement questions depend on it.
- Practice converting word equations to formula equations first, then balance.
keyPoints: Balance by counting atoms element-by-element; smallest whole-number coefficients win.
Combination: many → one. Decomposition: one → many.
More reactive metal displaces less reactive metal from its salt.
Precipitate = insoluble product in double displacement.
Oxidation and reduction always happen together (redox).
Silver chloride turns grey in light — photolytic decomposition.
Rancid chips packets are flushed with nitrogen.

notes.title: Real Numbers — Revision Notes
notes.content:
# Real Numbers — Revision Notes

## Introduction
Real numbers combine every rational and irrational number into one family, and this chapter builds the number toolbox you will use all through Class 10 board maths. Two big ideas drive the exam: the **Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic** (prime factorisation) and **irrationality proofs**.

## Key Concepts

### Euclid's Division Lemma
For any two positive integers a and b, there exist unique integers q (quotient) and r (remainder) such that a = bq + r, with 0 ≤ r < b. It is the formal way of saying "divide and write the remainder". It powers the **Euclid division algorithm**, a step-by-step method to compute the HCF of two numbers: keep dividing the divisor by the remainder until the remainder becomes 0; the last non-zero remainder is the HCF.

### Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic
Every composite number can be written as a product of primes, and this factorisation is unique apart from the order of factors. For example, 84 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 7, no matter how you start. This uniqueness is why HCF and LCM can be computed from prime factorisations: HCF takes the **lowest power** of common primes, LCM takes the **highest power** of all primes present.

### HCF × LCM relation
For any two positive integers a and b: HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b. Handy shortcut: find the HCF first, then divide a × b by it to get the LCM. Note this product rule is valid for **two** numbers only — for three numbers you must find each value separately.

### Irrational numbers
A number is irrational if it cannot be written as p/q with integers p, q (q ≠ 0). Their decimal expansions are non-terminating and non-repeating. The classic exam proof shows √2, √3 or √5 are irrational by contradiction: assume √2 = p/q in lowest terms, show both p and q must then be even, contradicting "lowest terms".

### Decimal expansion logic
For a rational p/q in lowest terms, the expansion terminates exactly when the prime factorisation of q contains only 2s and/or 5s; otherwise it repeats. This gives quick one-mark answers like "17/3125 terminates because 3125 = 5⁵".

## Example
Find HCF and LCM of 26 and 91.
- 26 = 2 × 13; 91 = 7 × 13.
- HCF = 13 (common prime, lowest power).
- LCM = 2 × 7 × 13 = 182 (all primes, highest power).
- Check: 13 × 182 = 2366 = 26 × 91 ✓

## Quick Revision
- HCF: product of common primes with lowest powers.
- LCM: product of all primes with highest powers.
- HCF × LCM = product of the two numbers.
- Every composite number has a unique prime factorisation.
- √2, √3, √5 are irrational; sums of rational + irrational are always irrational.
- p/q terminates ⇔ q (lowest form) has only 2s and 5s.
- Euclid's algorithm: last non-zero remainder = HCF.

## Exam Tips
- The 3-mark "prove √n is irrational" proof needs the "assume lowest terms → contradiction" structure; write every step.
- Word problems on bells/traffic lights/tanks circling together usually need **LCM**; splitting into groups needs **HCF**.
- Never skip writing the given/assumption lines in proofs — step marking rewards them.
- Practise mixed questions where HCF/LCM of three numbers is asked; the product shortcut fails there.
- Keep factorisation of numbers up to 100 memorised for speed.
keyPoints: HCF: product of common primes with lowest powers.
LCM: product of all primes with highest powers.
HCF × LCM = product of the two numbers.
Every composite number has a unique prime factorisation.
√2, √3, √5 are irrational; sums of rational + irrational are always irrational.
p/q terminates ⇔ q (lowest form) has only 2s and 5s.
Euclid's algorithm: last non-zero remainder = HCF.

questions.text: In a Young's double-slit experiment, the distance between the slits is 0.8 mm and the distance to the screen is 1.2 m. If the wavelength of light used is 600 nm, the distance between the first dark fringe and the central bright fringe is approximately:
questions.explanation: The position of the first dark fringe is given by y = λD/(2d), where λ is the wavelength, D is the distance to the screen, and d is the slit separation.

questions.text: A convex lens of focal length 20 cm is placed in contact with a concave lens of focal length 30 cm. The power of the combination is:
questions.explanation: The power of a lens combination is the sum of individual powers. P = P1 + P2 = 1/f1 + 1/f2 = 1/0.2 + 1/(-0.3) = 5 - 3.33 = 1.67 D

questions.text: A particle of mass m is executing simple harmonic motion with amplitude A and angular frequency ω. The average kinetic energy over one complete cycle is:
questions.explanation: In simple harmonic motion, the average kinetic energy over one complete cycle is half the maximum kinetic energy, which is (1/2) × (1/2)mω²A² = (1/4)mω²A².

questions.text: A radioactive substance has a half-life of 5 years. How much of the substance will remain after 20 years?
questions.explanation: After 20 years, which is 4 half-lives, the remaining amount is (1/2)^4 = 1/16 of the original amount.

questions.text: A solenoid of length 30 cm and radius 2 cm has 500 turns. If a current of 2 A flows through it, the magnetic field at the center of the solenoid is approximately:
questions.explanation: The magnetic field at the center of a solenoid is B = μ₀nI, where n is the number of turns per unit length. Here, n = 500/0.3 = 1667 turns/m, so B = 4π × 10⁻⁷ × 1667 × 2 ≈ 8.4 × 10⁻³ T.

questions.text: A capacitor of capacitance 10 μF is charged to a potential difference of 100 V and then connected to an uncharged capacitor of capacitance 20 μF. The common potential difference across the combination is:
questions.explanation: The common potential is given by V = Q_total / C_total = (C1V1)/(C1+C2) = (10×10⁻⁶×100)/(10×10⁻⁶+20×10⁻⁶) = 1000/30 ≈ 33.3 V.

questions.text: A proton and an electron are projected perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field with the same kinetic energy. The ratio of the radii of their circular paths is:
questions.explanation: The radius of the circular path is r = mv/(qB). Since kinetic energy K = (1/2)mv² is the same, r = √(2mK)/(qB). For the same K and B, r ∝ m/q. The mass ratio of proton to electron is approximately 1836:1, and both have the same magnitude of charge, so r_p:r_e = 1836:1.

questions.text: A transformer has 100 turns in the primary coil and 500 turns in the secondary coil. If the primary is connected to a 220 V AC supply, the voltage across the secondary coil is:
questions.explanation: In a transformer, the voltage ratio is equal to the turns ratio. V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p, so V_s = V_p × (N_s/N_p) = 220 × (500/100) = 1100 V.

questions.text: The work function of a metal is 4.2 eV. If light of wavelength 300 nm is incident on the metal, the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons is:
questions.explanation: The maximum kinetic energy is K_max = hν - φ = hc/λ - φ = (1240/300) - 4.2 = 4.13 - 4.2 = -0.07 eV. Since this is negative, no photoelectrons will be emitted.
questions.chapterName: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text: A particle moves along the x-axis according to the equation x = 4t³ - 3t² + 2t, where x is in meters and t is in seconds. The acceleration of the particle at t = 2 s is:
questions.explanation: The velocity is v = dx/dt = 12t² - 6t + 2, and acceleration is a = dv/dt = 24t - 6. At t = 2 s, a = 24×2 - 6 = 48 - 6 = 42 m/s².

questions.text: If A is a square matrix of order 3 and |A| = 5, then what is the value of |2A|?
questions.explanation: For a square matrix of order n, |kA| = k^n|A|, so here |2A| = 2^3 × 5 = 40.

questions.text: The function f(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 + 3x - 1 is
questions.explanation: f'(x) = 3x^2 - 6x + 3 = 3(x-1)^2 ≥ 0 for all x, with equality only at x=1, so f is strictly increasing.

questions.text: If the line x/a + y/b = 1 passes through the points (2,3) and (4,-1), then what is the value of a/b?
questions.explanation: Substituting the points gives 2/a + 3/b = 1 and 4/a - 1/b = 1. Solving these equations simultaneously yields a/b = 2.

questions.text: What is the area of the region bounded by the curve y = x^2, the x-axis, and the lines x = 0 and x = 2?
questions.explanation: The area is given by ∫₀² x^2 dx = [x^3/3]₀² = 8/3 - 0 = 8/3 sq. units.

questions.text: The general solution of the differential equation dy/dx = (x+y)/(x-y) is
questions.explanation: This is a homogeneous differential equation. Substituting y = vx and solving gives x^2 - y^2 = C as the solution.

questions.text: If a, b, c are in A.P. and b, c, d are in G.P., then what is the relationship between a, b, c, d?
questions.explanation: Since a, b, c are in A.P., 2b = a + c. Since b, c, d are in G.P., c^2 = bd. Solving these gives a^2 = d^2.

questions.text: The angle between the vectors a = 2i - j + k and b = i + 2j - k is
questions.explanation: The angle θ between two vectors is given by cosθ = (a·b)/(|a||b|) = (2-1-1)/(√6·√6) = 0, so θ = π/2.

questions.text: If the line x = 1 + t, y = 2 - t, z = 3 + 2t is perpendicular to the plane ax + by + cz = 0, then what is the value of a + b + c?
questions.explanation: The direction vector of the line is (1, -1, 2), which must be parallel to the normal vector (a, b, c) of the plane. Thus a = k, b = -k, c = 2k, so a + b + c = 2k.

questions.text: If f(x) = sin(x^2), then what is f'(x)?
questions.explanation: Using the chain rule, f'(x) = cos(x^2) · d/dx(x^2) = cos(x^2) · 2x = 2x cos(x^2).

questions.text: The value of the definite integral ∫₀^π (sin^4 x + cos^4 x) dx is
questions.explanation: Using the identity sin^4 x + cos^4 x = 1 - 2sin^2 x cos^2 x and simplifying, the integral evaluates to π/2.

questions.text: If A is a square matrix of order 3 and |A| = 5, then |adj(A)| is equal to:
questions.explanation: For a square matrix of order n, |adj(A)| = |A|^(n-1). Here n=3, so |adj(A)| = 5^(3-1) = 25.

questions.text: The value of the integral ∫(from 0 to π) sin^4(x) dx is:
questions.explanation: Using the reduction formula for sin^n(x), we get ∫(from 0 to π) sin^4(x) dx = 3π/8.

questions.text: The area of the region bounded by the curve y = x^2 and the line y = 4x - x^2 is:
questions.explanation: Find points of intersection (0,0) and (4,0), then integrate |x^2 - (4x - x^2)| from 0 to 4 to get 16/3 sq units.

questions.text: The distance between the planes 2x - 2y + z + 5 = 0 and 4x - 4y + 2z + 20 = 0 is:
questions.explanation: The planes are parallel. Divide the second equation by 2 and use the distance formula between parallel planes to get 5/3 units.

questions.text: The value of the limit lim(x→0) (sin(3x) - sin(x))/sin(5x) is:
questions.explanation: Using L'Hôpital's rule or standard limits, we get lim(x→0) (3cos(3x) - cos(x))/(5cos(5x)) = 2/5.

questions.text: The number of solutions of the equation sin(x) + cos(x) = 1 in the interval [0, 2π] is:
questions.explanation: Rewriting as √2 sin(x + π/4) = 1 gives x + π/4 = π/4 or 3π/4, leading to two solutions in [0, 2π].

questions.text: The equation of the tangent to the curve y = x^3 + 2x^2 - 5x + 3 at x = 1 is:
questions.explanation: Find dy/dx = 3x^2 + 4x - 5, evaluate at x=1 to get slope=2, then use point-slope form with (1,1) to get y = 4x - 3.

questions.text: The value of the determinant |[1, a, a^2], [1, b, b^2], [1, c, c^2]| is:
questions.explanation: This is a Vandermonde determinant, which evaluates to (a-b)(b-c)(c-a) for 3×3 matrix.

questions.text: The differential equation representing the family of curves y = ae^(2x) + be^(-3x) + c is:
questions.explanation: Differentiating three times and eliminating constants gives the characteristic equation r³ - r - 6 = 0, corresponding to the given DE.

questions.text: The value of the integral ∫(from 0 to ∞) x^2 e^(-x) dx is:
questions.explanation: Using integration by parts twice or recognizing it as Γ(3) = 2! = 2.

questions.text: विश्व की प्रथम महिला प्रधानमंत्री कौन थीं?
questions.explanation: इंदिरा गांधी विश्व की पहली महिला प्रधानमंत्री थीं जिन्होंने भारत में पद संभाला।

questions.text: हिंदी साहित्य में 'अंधेरे में' किस लेखक का प्रसिद्ध उपन्यास है?
questions.explanation: 'अंधेरे में' यशपाल द्वारा लिखा गया एक प्रसिद्ध उपन्यास है जो सामाजिक समस्याओं को उजागर करता है।

questions.text: महात्मा गांधी द्वारा 'हरिजन' शब्द का प्रयोग किस समाज के लिए किया गया था?
questions.explanation: महात्मा गांधी ने 'हरिजन' शब्द का प्रयोग अस्पृश्य समाज के लिए किया था और उन्हें समाज में उचित स्थान दिलाने के लिए कार्य किया।

questions.text: भारत के संविधान में राज्यपाल के पद पर कितन समय तक रहने की व्यवस्था है?
questions.explanation: भारत के संविधान के अनुच्छेद 156 के अनुसार, राज्यपाल का पद राष्ट्रपति की इच्छानुसार होता है और उसकी कोई निश्चित अवधि नहीं होती।

questions.text: हिंदी भाषा का प्राचीनतम ग्रंथ क्या है?
questions.explanation: सिद्धहेमशब्दानुशासन हिंदी भाषा का प्राचीनतम ज्ञात व्याकरण ग्रंथ है जिसकी रचना 9वीं शताब्दी में हुई थी।

questions.text: भारत के राष्ट्रपति द्वारा लागू किए गए आपातकाल की अवधि कितनी होती है?
questions.explanation: भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 352 के अनुसार, राष्ट्रपति द्वारा लागू किए गए आपातकाल की प्रारंभिक अवधि 6 महीने होती है।

questions.text: भारत में सबसे लंबी सीमा किस देश के साथ है?
questions.explanation: भारत की बांग्लादेश के साथ सबसे लंबी सीमा है जो लगभग 4,096 किलोमीटर लंबी है।

questions.text: हिंदी साहित्य में 'छायावाद' की नींव किसने रखी?
questions.explanation: जयशंकर प्रसाद को हिंदी साहित्य में छायावाद के प्रवर्तक माना जाता है जिन्होंने इस आंदोलन की नींव रखी।

questions.text: भारत के संविधान में 'डीपीएसपी' का क्या अर्थ है?
questions.explanation: डीपीएसपी का पूरा नाम डायरेक्ट प्रोडक्शन सपोर्ट प्राइस है जो कृषकों को उनकी फसलों की सीधी खरीद के लिए सरकार द्वारा दिए जाने वाले समर्थन मूल्य को दर्शाता है।

questions.text: भारत का राष्ट्रीय पशु क्या है?
questions.explanation: भारत का राष्ट्रीय पशु गाय है जिसे भारतीय संस्कृति में पवित्र माना जाता है।

questions.text: किस रचना में लेखक ने समाज की विकृतियों पर कटाक्ष किया है?
questions.explanation: प्रेमचंद के उपन्यास 'गोदान' में ग्रामीण समाज की विकृतियों और भ्रष्टाचार पर तीखा व्यंग्य किया गया है।

questions.text: 'अमर उजाला' किस लेखक की प्रसिद्ध रचना है?
questions.explanation: 'अमर उजाला' हरिवंश राय बच्चन का प्रसिद्ध उपन्यास है जिसमें भारतीय समाज की जटिलताओं का चित्रण है।

questions.text: काव्य में 'अनुप्रास' अलंकार का उदाहरण कौन सा है?
questions.explanation: 'अनुप्रास' अलंकार में एक ही वर्ण की पुनरावृत्ति होती है, जैसे 'बादल-बारिश' में 'ब' की आवृत्ति।

questions.text: 'मेरा भारत महान' कविता किस विषय पर आधारित है?
questions.explanation: यह कविता भारत की गौरवशाली इतिहास और संस्कृति का वर्णन करती है और देशभक्ति का भाव व्यक्त करती है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा 'अभिधा' अर्थ का उदाहरण नहीं है?
options: A) 'घर' शब्द से आवास का बोध होना
B) 'सागर' शब्द से विशाल जलराशि का बोध होना
C) 'सुख' शब्द से आनंद का बोध होना
D) 'गीत' शब्द से गाने की कला का बोध होना
questions.answer: D) 'गीत' शब्द से गाने की कला का बोध होना
questions.explanation: 'अभिधा' अर्थ में शब्द से उसका सीधा अर्थ बोध होता है, जबकि 'गीत' से गाने की कला का बोध 'लक्षणा' अर्थ का उदाहरण है।

questions.text: 'देव' शब्द का विलोम क्या है?
questions.explanation: 'देव' का विलोम 'असुर' है, क्योंकि देव देवता होते हैं और असुर दैत्य होते हैं।

questions.text: किस उपन्यास में 'आँखों के सामने' शीर्षक प्रसिद्ध पंक्तियाँ हैं?
questions.explanation: 'कैंडल इन द विंड' में 'आँखों के सामने' प्रसिद्ध पंक्तियाँ हैं जो दृश्यों की तीव्रता को दर्शाती हैं।

questions.text: काव्य में 'उपमा' अलंकार किस आधार पर काम करता है?
questions.explanation: 'उपमा' अलंकार में दो वस्तुओं के बीच समानता के आधार पर तुलना की जाती है।

questions.text: 'अंधेरे में एक दीया' किस लेखक की प्रसिद्ध रचना है?
questions.explanation: 'अंधेरे में एक दीया' फ़िराक़ गोरखपुरी की प्रसिद्ध कविता है जिसमें आशा और प्रकाश का प्रतीक है।

questions.text: किस शब्द में 'अनुस्वार' वर्ण प्रयुक्त है?
questions.explanation: 'अंगूर' में 'अनुस्वार' (ं) का प्रयोग हुआ है जो 'अ' और 'ग' के बीच स्वरग्रहण का प्रतीक है।

questions.text: In the sentence 'The committee has submitted its report,' the underlined word functions as a:
questions.explanation: The committee is the doer of the action 'submitted' and is the subject of the sentence.

questions.text: Which of the following sentences uses the subjunctive mood correctly?
options: A) If I was you, I would study harder.
B) If I were you, I would study harder.
C) If I am you, I would study harder.
D) If I have been you, I would study harder.
questions.answer: B) If I were you, I would study harder.
questions.explanation: The subjunctive mood is used for hypothetical situations, and 'were' is the correct form after 'if' when referring to the present.

questions.text: In the poem 'If—' by Rudyard Kipling, the central theme is primarily concerned with:
options: B) The qualities of ideal manhood
questions.answer: B) The qualities of ideal manhood
questions.explanation: The poem enumerates various virtues and qualities that constitute ideal manhood and moral integrity.

questions.text: The literary device used in the phrase 'the world is too much with us' in Wordsworth's sonnet is:
questions.explanation: The abstract concept of 'the world' is given human characteristics by being described as being 'too much with us'.

questions.text: In the novel 'The Invisible Man' by H.G. Wells, Griffin's invisibility symbolizes:
options: B) The alienation of the individual
C) The power of the human mind
D) The dangers of nuclear energy
questions.answer: B) The alienation of the individual
questions.explanation: Griffin's invisibility isolates him from society, highlighting the theme of an individual's alienation from the community.

questions.text: The phrase 'to bite the bullet' means:
options: B) To endure a painful or difficult situation with courage
D) To make a quick decision
questions.answer: B) To endure a painful or difficult situation with courage
questions.explanation: This idiom originates from the practice of having patients bite on a bullet during surgical procedures without anesthesia.

questions.text: In the play 'The Merchant of Venice,' the character Portia is famous for her:
questions.explanation: Portia is renowned for her cleverness, particularly in the trial scene where she outwits Shylock using his own arguments against him.

questions.text: The literary term 'epistolary' refers to a novel written in the form of:
questions.explanation: An epistolary novel is one that is written as a series of documents, typically letters, exchanged between characters.

questions.text: In the sentence 'Having finished his homework, he went out to play,' the underlined phrase is a:
questions.explanation: The phrase 'Having finished his homework' modifies the verb 'went' and tells us when the action occurred.

questions.text: The stream of consciousness technique in modernist literature is best exemplified by:
questions.explanation: Woolf extensively employed stream of consciousness in novels like 'Mrs. Dalloway' to portray the inner thoughts of characters.

questions.text: In the sentence 'The committee are divided in their opinions,' the verb 'are' agrees with which grammatical concept?
options: A) The collective noun functioning as a plural
D) The concept of uncountable nouns
questions.answer: A) The collective noun functioning as a plural
questions.explanation: Here, 'committee' is treated as a plural entity as the members are considered individually, hence 'are' is used instead of 'is'.

questions.text: Identify the figure of speech in the line: 'The world is too much with us; late and soon, Getting and spending, we lay waste our powers.'
questions.explanation: The poet attributes human qualities ('getting and spending') to abstract concepts representing human activities.

questions.text: Which of the following sentences correctly uses the subjunctive mood?
options: A) If I was you, I would study harder.
B) If I were you, I would study harder.
C) If I am you, I would study harder.
D) If I will be you, I would study harder.
questions.answer: B) If I were you, I would study harder.
questions.explanation: The subjunctive mood is used for hypothetical situations, and 'were' is the correct form after 'if' when expressing something contrary to fact.

questions.text: In the context of writing a formal letter, what is the purpose of the 'subject' line?
options: A) To provide the sender's address
B) To indicate the topic of the letter
C) To include the date of writing
D) To mention the recipient's designation
questions.answer: B) To indicate the topic of the letter
questions.explanation: The subject line helps the recipient quickly understand the content or purpose of the letter.

questions.text: What literary device is employed in the phrase: 'The camel is the ship of the desert'?
questions.explanation: This is a metaphor as it directly compares the camel to a ship without using 'like' or 'as'.

questions.text: In the sentence 'Neither of the boys has completed his homework,' the pronoun 'his' refers to which grammatical concept?
questions.explanation: 'Neither' is a distributive pronoun, and the pronoun 'his' agrees with it in number and gender.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of an oxymoron?
questions.explanation: An oxymoron combines two contradictory terms, and 'deafening silence' places the contradictory concepts of sound and lack of sound together.

questions.text: In a debate, what is the primary purpose of the 'rebuttal'?
options: B) To present arguments in favor of the motion
C) To counter the opposing team's arguments
D) To summarize the main points
questions.answer: C) To counter the opposing team's arguments
questions.explanation: A rebuttal specifically addresses and refutes the arguments presented by the opposing side in a debate.

questions.text: Which of the following sentences demonstrates correct use of the participle?
options: A) Walking in the park, a snake bit him.
B) Walking in the park, he was bitten by a snake.
C) Being walked in the park, a snake bit him.
D) Having walked in the park, a snake bit him.
questions.answer: B) Walking in the park, he was bitten by a snake.
questions.explanation: This sentence correctly uses the participle 'walking' to modify the subject 'he' without creating a dangling modifier.

questions.text: In the context of writing a story, what is the 'denouement'?
options: A) The introduction of characters and setting
B) The series of events that build tension
C) The final resolution of the plot
questions.answer: C) The final resolution of the plot
questions.explanation: The denouement is the conclusion of a story where the outcome of the conflict is revealed and loose ends are tied up.

questions.text: Which of the following is a characteristic of a perfectly competitive market?
options: A) Few sellers dominate the market
questions.explanation: In perfect competition, all firms sell identical products, making them perfect substitutes for consumers.
questions.chapterName: Forms of Market and Price Determination

questions.text: The Marginal Propensity to Consume (MPC) is defined as:
options: A) The ratio of total consumption to total income
B) The change in consumption divided by the change in income
C) The ratio of savings to income
D) The additional consumption from an additional unit of wealth
questions.answer: B) The change in consumption divided by the change in income
questions.explanation: MPC measures how much consumption changes when income changes by one unit.

questions.text: When the Reserve Bank of India purchases government securities from the market, it leads to:
options: D) No change in money supply
questions.explanation: Open market operations where RBI buys securities inject money into the economy, increasing the money supply.

questions.text: In the context of balance of payments, a current account surplus indicates:
options: A) A country is importing more goods than it exports
B) A country is exporting more goods than it imports
questions.answer: B) A country is exporting more goods than it imports
questions.explanation: A current account surplus means a country's exports of goods and services exceed its imports.

questions.text: The law of diminishing marginal utility states that:
options: A) Total utility increases at a decreasing rate
B) Marginal utility decreases as consumption increases
D) Total utility decreases with each additional unit consumed
questions.answer: B) Marginal utility decreases as consumption increases
questions.explanation: As more units of a good are consumed, the additional satisfaction from each successive unit tends to decrease.

questions.text: If the price elasticity of demand for a good is -2.5, it indicates:
questions.explanation: A price elasticity of demand greater than 1 (in absolute value) indicates elastic demand where quantity demanded is responsive to price changes.

questions.text: In the Keynesian cross model, the equilibrium level of income occurs where:
options: B) Aggregate demand equals aggregate supply
questions.answer: B) Aggregate demand equals aggregate supply
questions.explanation: In the Keynesian cross model, equilibrium is achieved when total spending (aggregate demand) equals total output (aggregate supply).

questions.text: The Phillips curve illustrates the relationship between:
options: C) Government spending and tax revenue
questions.explanation: The Phillips curve shows an inverse relationship between the rate of inflation and the rate of unemployment in the short run.

questions.text: A firm will shut down in the short run if:
options: A) Price is less than average total cost
B) Price is less than average variable cost
C) Price is less than marginal cost
D) Price is less than average fixed cost
questions.answer: B) Price is less than average variable cost
questions.explanation: In the short run, a firm will shut down if it cannot cover its variable costs, as continuing production would increase losses.

questions.text: The concept of 'circular flow of income' in an economy demonstrates:
options: A) How money circulates between households and firms
B) How taxes are collected by the government
C) How international trade affects the economy
D) How savings are invested in the economy
questions.answer: A) How money circulates between households and firms
questions.explanation: The circular flow model illustrates the continuous movement of money and goods between households (factors of production) and firms (producers of goods and services).

questions.text: When the marginal propensity to consume is 0.8, the value of the multiplier will be:
questions.explanation: The multiplier is calculated as 1/(1-MPC), which in this case is 1/(1-0.8) = 1/0.2 = 5.

questions.text: Which of the following is a direct tax?
questions.explanation: Income tax is a direct tax as it is levied directly on the income of individuals and organizations, whereas GST, excise duty, and customs duty are indirect taxes.

questions.text: If the price of a commodity increases by 20% and the quantity demanded decreases by 10%, the price elasticity of demand is:
questions.explanation: Price elasticity of demand is calculated as the percentage change in quantity demanded divided by the percentage change in price, which in this case is -10%/20% = -0.5 (absolute value is 0.5).

questions.text: Which of the following is a characteristic of a perfectly competitive market?
questions.explanation: Perfectly competitive markets have many sellers offering identical (homogeneous) products, no price control, and no barriers to entry.

questions.text: When total revenue is at its maximum, marginal revenue is:
questions.explanation: Marginal revenue is the change in total revenue from selling one additional unit. At the point where total revenue is maximized, selling one more unit does not change total revenue, making marginal revenue zero.

questions.text: In the short run, if a firm's average variable cost exceeds its price, the firm should:
questions.explanation: If price is below average variable cost, the firm cannot cover its variable costs and should temporarily shut down to minimize losses in the short run.

questions.text: Which of the following would shift the supply curve of a commodity to the right?
options: C) Expectation of higher future prices
questions.explanation: A decrease in input prices reduces production costs, making it profitable to supply more at each price level, thus shifting the supply curve to the right.

questions.text: The Phillips curve illustrates a relationship between:
questions.explanation: The Phillips curve shows an inverse relationship between inflation and unemployment in the short run, suggesting that lower unemployment is associated with higher inflation.

questions.text: If the economy is operating at a point inside the production possibility frontier, it indicates:
questions.explanation: When an economy operates inside its production possibility frontier, it indicates that resources are not fully utilized, leading to unemployment or underemployment.

questions.text: In the context of the balance of payments, a current account deficit implies:
options: D) No change in foreign exchange reserves
questions.explanation: A current account deficit occurs when a country's imports of goods, services, and transfers exceed its exports, indicating a net outflow of domestic currency.

questions.text: Which of the following compounds exhibits geometrical isomerism?
questions.explanation: 1,2-Dichloroethene can exist as cis and trans isomers due to restricted rotation around the carbon-carbon double bond.

questions.text: The rate of a reaction doubles when the concentration of reactant is doubled. The order of the reaction is:
questions.explanation: When the rate of reaction is directly proportional to the concentration of reactant, it follows first-order kinetics.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a Lewis acid?
questions.explanation: NH3 has a lone pair of electrons and can donate it, making it a Lewis base rather than a Lewis acid.

questions.text: The molar conductivity of a 0.1 M KCl solution at 25°C is 129 S cm² mol⁻¹. The conductivity of the solution is:
questions.explanation: Conductivity (κ) = Molar conductivity (Λm) × Concentration (c) = 129 S cm² mol⁻¹ × 0.1 mol L⁻¹ = 0.0129 S cm⁻¹.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the hybridization of carbon in diamond and graphite is correct?
options: C) Diamond has sp³ and graphite has sp² hybridization
D) Diamond has sp² and graphite has sp³ hybridization
questions.answer: C) Diamond has sp³ and graphite has sp² hybridization
questions.explanation: In diamond, each carbon is tetrahedrally bonded to four other carbons (sp³ hybridization), while in graphite, each carbon is trigonal planar bonded to three other carbons (sp² hybridization).

questions.text: The standard reduction potential of Cu²⁺/Cu is +0.34 V. The standard reduction potential of Cu²⁺/Cu⁺ is +0.15 V. The standard reduction potential of Cu⁺/Cu is:
questions.explanation: Using the formula: ΔG° = -nFE° and the relationship between the three half-reactions, we can calculate E° for Cu⁺/Cu as +0.52 V.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a thermosetting polymer?
questions.explanation: Bakelite is a thermosetting polymer that undergoes irreversible curing when heated, forming a cross-linked structure.

questions.text: The pH of 0.01 M HCl solution is:
questions.explanation: HCl is a strong acid that dissociates completely, so [H⁺] = 0.01 M, and pH = -log(0.01) = 2.

questions.text: Which of the following complexes will show geometrical isomerism?
questions.explanation: [Co(NH3)4Cl2]⁺ has a square planar geometry with two Cl ligands that can be arranged in cis and trans positions.

questions.text: The rate constant of a first-order reaction is 0.693 min⁻¹. The half-life of the reaction is:
questions.explanation: For a first-order reaction, half-life (t₁/₂) = 0.693/k, where k is the rate constant. Therefore, t₁/₂ = 0.693/0.693 = 1.0 min.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a cancerous cell?
questions.explanation: Cancerous cells lose contact inhibition, allowing them to pile up on each other, which is not a characteristic of normal cells.

questions.text: During DNA replication, the enzyme that joins the Okazaki fragments is:
questions.explanation: DNA ligase joins the Okazaki fragments on the lagging strand by forming phosphodiester bonds between them.

questions.text: In the human menstrual cycle, the hormone responsible for the maintenance of the endometrium is:
questions.explanation: Progesterone is primarily responsible for maintaining the endometrium during the secretory phase of the menstrual cycle.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a part of the electron transport chain?
questions.explanation: ATP synthase is not part of the electron transport chain but utilizes the proton gradient created by it to synthesize ATP.

questions.text: The phenomenon where a gene has multiple phenotypic effects is called:
questions.explanation: Pleiotropy occurs when a single gene influences multiple phenotypic traits, as seen in sickle cell anemia.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a function of the liver?
questions.explanation: Insulin is produced by the beta cells of the pancreas, not by the liver, although the liver does respond to insulin.

questions.text: In Mendelian genetics, when two heterozygous individuals are crossed, the phenotypic ratio in the F2 generation is:
questions.explanation: In a monohybrid cross between two heterozygous individuals, the phenotypic ratio in the F2 generation is 3:1 for dominant to recessive traits.

questions.text: The enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of pyruvate to acetyl CoA is:
questions.explanation: Pyruvate dehydrogenase catalyzes the conversion of pyruvate to acetyl CoA, a key step linking glycolysis to the Krebs cycle.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a post-translational modification of proteins?
questions.explanation: Transcription is the process of RNA synthesis from DNA and is not a post-translational modification of proteins.

questions.text: The concept of 'one gene-one enzyme' was proposed by:
options: C) George Beadle and Edward Tatum
questions.answer: C) George Beadle and Edward Tatum
questions.explanation: Beadle and Tatum proposed the 'one gene-one enzyme' hypothesis based on their experiments with Neurospora crassa.

questions.text: A particle moves in a circular path of radius 5 m with a constant speed of 10 m/s. The magnitude of its acceleration is
questions.explanation: For uniform circular motion, acceleration is given by a = v²/r = (10)²/5 = 20 m/s², directed toward the center.

questions.text: A block of mass 2 kg is placed on a rough horizontal surface. The coefficient of static friction is 0.3. What is the maximum horizontal force that can be applied to the block without causing it to move?
questions.explanation: Maximum static friction force is f_s = μ_s × N = 0.3 × 2 × 9.8 = 5.88 N, where N is the normal force equal to weight on a horizontal surface.

questions.text: A ball is thrown vertically upward with a velocity of 20 m/s. What will be its velocity after 2 seconds? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Using v = u - gt, we get v = 20 - 10 × 2 = 0 m/s, meaning the ball reaches its maximum height at this time.

questions.text: A car of mass 1000 kg is moving with a velocity of 10 m/s. If it is brought to rest in 5 seconds, what is the average retarding force?
questions.explanation: Using F = ma, where a = (v-u)/t = (0-10)/5 = -2 m/s², so F = 1000 × (-2) = -2000 N (negative sign indicates retarding force).

questions.text: A stone is dropped from a height of 100 m. What will be its velocity just before hitting the ground? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Using v² = u² + 2gh = 0 + 2 × 10 × 100 = 2000, so v = √2000 ≈ 44.7 m/s (closest to 40 m/s).

questions.text: A particle moves along a straight line with a velocity given by v = 4t³ - 3t² + 2. What is its acceleration at t = 1 second?
questions.explanation: Acceleration is the derivative of velocity with respect to time: a = dv/dt = 12t² - 6t. At t = 1 s, a = 12(1)² - 6(1) = 6 m/s².

questions.text: A block of mass 5 kg is placed on an inclined plane making an angle of 30° with the horizontal. The coefficient of kinetic friction is 0.2. What is the acceleration of the block down the plane? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: The net force down the plane is mg sinθ - μ mg cosθ = 5 × 10 × sin30° - 0.2 × 5 × 10 × cos30° = 25 - 8.66 = 16.34 N. Acceleration = F/m = 16.34/5 ≈ 3.27 m/s² (closest to 3 m/s²).

questions.text: A satellite is orbiting the Earth at a height of 3600 km above the Earth's surface. If the radius of the Earth is 6400 km, what is the ratio of the gravitational acceleration at this height to that on the Earth's surface?
questions.explanation: Gravitational acceleration is inversely proportional to the square of the distance from the center. The distance from center at height is 6400 + 3600 = 10000 km, compared to 6400 km at surface. The ratio is (6400/10000)² = (16/25)² = 1/16.

questions.text: A particle is moving in a circular path of radius 2 m with a constant angular velocity of 5 rad/s. What is the linear velocity of the particle?
questions.explanation: Linear velocity v = rω = 2 × 5 = 10 m/s, where r is the radius and ω is the angular velocity.

questions.text: A force F = (3i + 4j) N acts on a particle of mass 1 kg. What is the magnitude of the acceleration of the particle?
questions.explanation: The magnitude of the force is |F| = √(3² + 4²) = 5 N. Using F = ma, the magnitude of acceleration is a = F/m = 5/1 = 5 m/s².

questions.text: If the function f(x) = 3x² - 2x + 5 is defined from R to R, then which of the following statements is true about this function?
options: A) It is one-one but not onto
B) It is onto but not one-one
C) It is neither one-one nor onto
D) It is both one-one and onto
questions.answer: A) It is one-one but not onto
questions.explanation: The function is a quadratic with a positive leading coefficient, so it has a minimum point and is not one-one. It is also not onto as it doesn't cover all real values (range is [4, ∞)).

questions.text: The value of sin(π/12) × cos(π/12) is equal to:
questions.explanation: Using the double angle identity sin(2θ) = 2sinθcosθ, we get sin(π/12)cos(π/12) = (1/2)sin(π/6) = (1/2)(1/2) = 1/4.

questions.text: If a matrix A has order 3×2 and matrix B has order 2×4, then the order of matrix AB is:
questions.explanation: When multiplying matrices, the resulting matrix has the same number of rows as the first matrix and the same number of columns as the second matrix.

questions.text: The derivative of logₑ(sin x) with respect to x is:
questions.explanation: Using the chain rule, d/dx[log(sin x)] = (1/sin x) × cos x = cos x/sin x = cot x.

questions.text: If the vectors a = 2i + 3j - k and b = i - 2j + 3k, then the angle between them is:
questions.explanation: The dot product a·b = (2)(1) + (3)(-2) + (-1)(3) = 2 - 6 - 3 = -7. Since a·b = |a||b|cosθ and a·b = 0, the angle is 90°.

questions.text: The value of ∫(x³ + 2x)dx from 0 to 1 is:
questions.explanation: Integrating term by term, we get (x⁴/4 + x²) evaluated from 0 to 1 = (1/4 + 1) - (0 + 0) = 5/4.

questions.text: If the complex number z = 1 + i, then the value of z² + z̄² is:
questions.explanation: First, z² = (1 + i)² = 1 + 2i + i² = 2i. The conjugate z̄ = 1 - i, so z̄² = (1 - i)² = 1 - 2i + i² = -2i. Therefore, z² + z̄² = 2i - 2i = 0.

questions.text: The general solution of the differential equation dy/dx = y/x is:
questions.explanation: This is a separable differential equation. Separating variables gives dy/y = dx/x, and integrating both sides gives ln|y| = ln|x| + c, which simplifies to y = kx.

questions.text: If the binomial expansion of (1 + x)ⁿ has coefficients in the ratio 1:3:3 for the first three terms, then n is equal to:
questions.explanation: The coefficients are C(n,0):C(n,1):C(n,2) = 1:n:n(n-1)/2. Setting n = 3 gives the ratio 1:3:3, which matches the given ratio.

questions.text: The value of lim(x→0) (sin x - x)/x³ is:
questions.explanation: Using L'Hôpital's rule three times: first derivative gives (cos x - 1)/3x², second gives -sin x/6x, third gives -cos x/6. Evaluating at x=0 gives -1/6.

questions.text: काव्य में 'अलंकार' का क्या महत्व है?
options: A) भावों को अधिक सुंदर बनाना
D) गद्य को पद्य में बदलना
questions.answer: A) भावों को अधिक सुंदर बनाना
questions.explanation: अलंकार काव्य को सुंदरता प्रदान करते हैं और भावों को अधिक प्रभावशाली बनाते हैं।

questions.text: तुलसीदास द्वारा रचित 'रामचरितमानस' का मुख्य भाषा क्या है?
questions.explanation: तुलसीदास ने 'रामचरितमानस' मुख्य रूप से अवधी भाषा में लिखा है, जो उनके समय की लोकप्रिय भाषा थी।

questions.text: महात्मा गांधी द्वारा संपादित 'हरिजन' पत्रिका का मुख्य उद्देश्य क्या था?
options: B) अछूतों की समस्याओं पर चर्चा
C) गांधी जी के�िचारों का प्रचार
D) ग्रामीण विकास के लिए जागरूकता
questions.answer: B) अछूतों की समस्याओं पर चर्चा
questions.explanation: 'हरिजन' पत्रिका मुख्य रूप से अछूतों की सामाजिक स्थिति को सुधारने और उनके अधिकारों के लिए संघर्ष करने के लिए प्रकाशित की गई थी।

questions.text: भारतेन्दु हरिश्चंद्र के अनुसार हिंदी साहित्य का 'आधुनिक युग' कब से शुरू हुआ?
options: C) भारतेन्दु के जन्म के बाद
questions.explanation: भारतेन्दु हरिश्चंद्र के अनुसार हिंदी साहित्य का आधुनिक युग 19वीं शताब्दी की शुरुआत से शुरू हुआ, जब भाषा में नवजागरण आया।

questions.text: श्री हरिवंशराय बच्चन के 'मधुशाला' में 'मदिरा' का प्रतीक क्या है?
questions.explanation: 'मधुशाला' में 'मदिरा' का प्रतीक काव्य है, जो जीवन की मीठी और कड़ी बातों का प्रतिनिधित्व करता है।

questions.text: हिंदी में 'अनुप्रास अलंकार' का उदाहरण कौन सा है?
questions.explanation: अनुप्रास अलंकार में एक ही व्यंजन का बार-बार प्रयोग होता है, जैसे 'रजनी रजनी रजकरे' में 'र' का बार-बार प्रयोग।

questions.text: प्रेमचंद की कहानी 'गोदान' का मुख्य विषय क्या है?
questions.explanation: 'गोदान' में प्रेमचंद ने सामाजिक अन्याय, गरीबी और जातिप्रथा जैसी समस्याओं को उजागर किया है।

questions.text: हिंदी भाषा में 'छांदस' शब्द का क्या अर्थ है?
questions.explanation: छांदस शब्द संस्कृत से आया है और इसका अर्थ पद्य या छंद वाला साहित्य है।

questions.text: 'बिहारी' की 'सतसई' में किस प्रकार के भावों का प्रधानता है?
questions.explanation: बिहारी की 'सतसई' में श्रृंगार रस की प्रधानता है, जो प्रेम और रूप के विभिन्न अवस्थाओं का वर्णन करता है।

questions.text: कबीर दास के दोहों में कौन सा दार्शनिक तत्व प्रमुख है?
questions.explanation: कबीर के दोहों में ज्ञान का वर्णन प्रमुख है, जो सत्य और मोक्ष की ओर इशारा करता है।

questions.text: 'अनुच्छेद' शब्द का सही व्याख्या क्या है?
options: A) किसी विषय पर लिखा गया छोटा निबंध
C) किसी विषय का संक्षिप्त विवरण
D) किसी गद्य ग्रंथ का एक भाग
questions.answer: D) किसी गद्य ग्रंथ का एक भाग
questions.explanation: 'अनुच्छेद' शब्द का अर्थ है किसी गद्य ग्रंथ या लेख का एक खंड या भाग जिसमें कोई विशेष विचार प्रस्तुत किया जाता है।

questions.text: 'विराम चिह्न' किस प्रकार के वर्णों के प्रयोग से बनते हैं?
questions.explanation: विराम चिह्न हिंदी वर्णमाला के किसी भी वर्ण से नहीं बनते, बल्कि वे अलग-अलग चिह्न होते हैं जो वाक्य में विश्राम या अन्य भाव दिखाने के काम आते हैं।

questions.text: 'अलंकार' क्या है?
options: A) काव्य का सुंदर वस्तुओं का वर्णन
B) काव्य में अलंकृत भाषा का प्रयोग
C) काव्य में अलफ़ाज़ की सुंदरता बढ़ाने वाले उपाय
D) काव्य में छंद का प्रयोग
questions.answer: C) काव्य में अलफ़ाज़ की सुंदरता बढ़ाने वाले उपाय
questions.explanation: अलंकार वे उपाय हैं जो काव्य के अलफ़ाज़ (शब्दों) की सुंदरता और आकर्षण को बढ़ाते हैं। ये भावों को अधिक प्रभावशाली बनाने में मदद करते हैं।

questions.text: 'अनुप्रास अलंकार' का उदाहरण कौन सा है?
questions.explanation: अनुप्रास अलंकार में एक ही वर्ण का बार-बार प्रयोग होता है। इस वाक्य में 'ब' वर्ण का बार-बार प्रयोग हुआ है - 'बादल', 'बरसे', 'बरवाई'।

questions.text: 'उपमा अलंकार' में क्या होता है?
options: A) दो वस्तुओं की तुला की जाती है
B) किसी वस्तु का वर्णन किया जाता है
C) किसी वस्तु का विस्तार से वर्णन किया जाता है
D) किसी वस्तु का अतिशयोक्तिपूर्ण वर्णन किया जाता है
questions.answer: A) दो वस्तुओं की तुला की जाती है
questions.explanation: उपमा अलंकार में एक वस्तु का दूसरी वस्तु से तुलना करके उसका वर्णन किया जाता है, जैसे 'चेहरा चाँद की तरह सूफ़ीदार'।

questions.text: 'छंद' क्या है?
options: D) काव्य में लय और ताल का नियमित प्रयोग
questions.answer: D) काव्य में लय और ताल का नियमित प्रयोग
questions.explanation: छंद का अर्थ है काव्य में लय और ताल का नियमित प्रयोग जो कविता को सुनने में सुंदर बनाता है। यह वर्णों की संख्या और उनके विन्यास पर निर्भर करता है।

questions.text: 'अन्त्यानुप्रास अलंकार' का उदाहरण कौन सा है?
questions.explanation: अन्त्यानुप्रास अलंकार में एक ही वर्ण के अंत में आने से उसकी लय बनती है। इस वाक्य में 'आ' वर्ण के अंत में आने से लय बनी है - 'राधा', 'नागर', 'नगरी'।

questions.text: 'शब्दालंकार' क्या है?
options: A) शब्दों की सुंदरता बढ़ाने वाले अलंकार
B) अर्थों की सुंदरता बढ़ाने वाले अलंकार
C) छंदों की सुंदरता बढ़ाने वाले अलंकार
D) भावों की सुंदरता बढ़ाने वाले अलंकार
questions.answer: A) शब्दों की सुंदरता बढ़ाने वाले अलंकार
questions.explanation: शब्दालंकार वे अलंकार हैं जो काव्य में शब्दों की सुंदरता और आकर्षण को बढ़ाते हैं। इनमें अनुप्रास, यमक आदि शामिल हैं।

questions.text: 'अतिशयोक्ति अलंकार' क्या है?
options: A) किसी वस्तु का अतिशय रूप से वर्णन
B) किसी वस्तु का वास्तविक वर्णन
C) किसी वस्तु का संक्षिप्त वर्णन
D) किसी वस्तु का तुलनात्मक वर्णन
questions.answer: A) किसी वस्तु का अतिशय रूप से वर्णन
questions.explanation: अतिशयोक्ति अलंकार में किसी वस्तु, भाव या स्थिति का अतिशय रूप से वर्णन किया जाता है, जैसे 'आँखों में पानी भर आ गया'।

questions.text: 'यमक अलंकार' क्या है?
options: A) एक ही शब्द का अलग-अलग अर्थ में प्रयोग
B) एक ही अर्थ का अलग-अलग शब्द से प्रयोग
C) एक ही वर्ण का बार-बार प्रयोग
D) एक ही वाक्य में अनेक अलंकार का प्रयोग
questions.answer: A) एक ही शब्द का अलग-अलग अर्थ में प्रयोग
questions.explanation: यमक अलंकार में एक ही शब्द का अलग-अलग अर्थ में प्रयोग किया जाता है, जैसे 'राम राम राम' में 'राम' का अलग-अलग अर्थ।

questions.text: In the sentence 'The committee has submitted its report,' the underlined word functions as a:
questions.explanation: The word 'committee' is a collective noun, which is a type of noun that refers to a group of individuals.

questions.text: Which of the following sentences correctly uses the subjunctive mood?
options: A) If I was you, I would study harder.
B) If I were you, I would study harder.
C) If I am you, I would study harder.
D) If I will be you, I would study harder.
questions.answer: B) If I were you, I would study harder.
questions.explanation: The subjunctive mood is used for hypothetical situations and requires 'were' instead of 'was' for all subjects.

questions.text: The literary device used in the phrase 'The world is a stage' is:
questions.explanation: A metaphor is a figure of speech that makes a direct comparison between two unlike things without using 'like' or 'as'.

questions.text: Which of the following sentences contains an example of zeugma?
options: A) She lost her way and her temper.
B) The sun rose and the birds sang.
C) He was tall, dark, and handsome.
D) The rain fell and the wind blew.
questions.answer: A) She lost her way and her temper.
questions.explanation: Zeugma is a figure of speech in which a word applies to more than two others in different senses, as in 'lost' applying to both 'way' and 'temper'.

questions.text: In the sentence 'The book that you lent me was fascinating,' the underlined clause is:
questions.explanation: An adjective clause modifies a noun or pronoun, in this case, it describes 'the book'.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a paradox?
options: A) Actions speak louder than words.
B) The more you learn, the less you know.
C) Time and tide wait for no man.
D) A stitch in time saves nine.
questions.answer: B) The more you learn, the less you know.
questions.explanation: A paradox is a statement that appears self-contradictory but reveals a deeper truth, as in this statement about knowledge.

questions.text: The word 'ephemeral' means:
questions.explanation: Ephemeral means lasting for a very short time; transitory.

questions.text: In the sentence 'Not only did he finish the project, but he also received an award,' the correct grammatical structure is:
questions.explanation: The sentence uses parallel structure by maintaining the same grammatical form for 'did finish' and 'received'.

questions.text: Which of the following sentences contains an example of anastrophe?
options: A) The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.
B) To the lighthouse, we sailed with hope in our hearts.
C) The boy ran quickly to the store.
D) With this ring, I thee wed.
questions.answer: B) To the lighthouse, we sailed with hope in our hearts.
questions.explanation: Anastrophe is the inversion of the normal order of words in a sentence, as in placing 'to the lighthouse' at the beginning.

questions.text: The term 'bildungsroman' refers to a:
options: A) Type of novel that follows the moral and psychological growth of the protagonist
B) Type of poem that tells a story
C) Type of play that deals with tragedy
D) Type of essay that argues a point
questions.answer: A) Type of novel that follows the moral and psychological growth of the protagonist
questions.explanation: A bildungsroman is a literary genre that focuses on the psychological and moral growth of the protagonist from youth to adulthood.

questions.text: In the sentence 'The old house creaked mournfully in the wind,' what literary device is used?
questions.explanation: The house is given human qualities by describing it as 'creaking mournfully,' which is a form of personification.

questions.text: Which of the following sentences uses the subjunctive mood correctly?
options: A) If I was you, I would study harder.
B) I wish I was taller.
C) If I were rich, I would buy a yacht.
D) She suggested that he comes early.
questions.answer: C) If I were rich, I would buy a yacht.
questions.explanation: The subjunctive mood is used for hypothetical situations, and 'were' is the correct form to use with 'I' in such cases.

questions.text: In the poem 'If—' by Rudyard Kipling, what does the phrase 'If you can meet with Triumph and Disaster And treat those two impostors just the same' suggest?
options: A) Success and failure are equally important
B) One should never experience either success or failure
C) Only triumph matters in life
D) Disaster should be avoided at all costs
questions.answer: A) Success and failure are equally important
questions.explanation: The poet advises treating both triumph and disaster with equanimity, suggesting that one should not be overly elated by success or dejected by failure.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a synecdoche?
options: A) The pen is mightier than the sword
D) He is a tiger in battle
questions.explanation: Synecdoche is a figure of speech where a part is used to represent the whole, as in using 'hands' to represent sailors or workers.

questions.text: Identify the sentence with correct subject-verb agreement:
options: A) The committee are divided on this issue.
B) Neither of the boys have submitted their assignment.
C) The United Nations has its headquarters in New York.
D) A number of students is absent today.
questions.answer: C) The United Nations has its headquarters in New York.
questions.explanation: Collective nouns like 'United Nations' take a singular verb when treated as a single entity, which is the case here.

questions.text: In the play 'The Merchant of Venice', what does Portia's speech about 'the quality of mercy' emphasize?
options: A) The importance of justice in society
B) Mercy as a divine attribute that humans should cultivate
C) The futility of legal systems
D) The superiority of mercy over love
questions.answer: B) Mercy as a divine attribute that humans should cultivate
questions.explanation: Portia's famous speech argues that mercy is an elevated quality that humans should strive to embody, as it 'blesseth him that gives and him that takes.'

questions.text: Which of the following sentences contains an example of zeugma?
options: A) She lost her book and her temper.
B) He opened the door and his heart.
C) The sun rose and the birds sang.
D) She wore a beautiful dress and a smile.
questions.answer: B) He opened the door and his heart.
questions.explanation: Zeugma is a figure of speech in which a word applies to two others in different senses, as 'opened' applies to both 'door' (physically) and 'heart' (metaphorically).

questions.text: Choose the sentence with correct use of the past perfect tense:
options: A) She has finished her homework before dinner.
B) They have been living here since 2010.
C) He had already left when I arrived.
D) She will have completed the project by Friday.
questions.answer: C) He had already left when I arrived.
questions.explanation: The past perfect tense is used to indicate an action completed before another past action, which is correctly used in this sentence.

questions.text: In the poem 'The Laburnum Top', what does the bird symbolize?
questions.explanation: The bird represents life and vitality as it brings movement, sound, and energy to the otherwise still and silent laburnum tree.

questions.text: Which of the following sentences correctly uses the word 'enormity'?
options: A) The enormity of the mountain was breathtaking.
B) She was shocked by the enormity of the crime.
C) He described the enormity of the delicious meal.
D) The enormity of the problem was easily solved.
questions.answer: B) She was shocked by the enormity of the crime.
questions.explanation: 'Enormity' refers to extreme wickedness or outrageousness, not size or magnitude, making it appropriate only when referring to morally reprehensible acts.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the concept of 'opportunity cost' in economics?
options: A) The total cost of producing a good
B) The cost of the next best alternative foregone
D) The fixed cost of production
questions.answer: B) The cost of the next best alternative foregone
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost represents the value of the next best alternative that must be given up to obtain something else.

questions.text: In the production possibility curve, the slope represents:
options: B) The opportunity cost of producing one good in terms of the other
questions.answer: B) The opportunity cost of producing one good in terms of the other
questions.explanation: The slope of the production possibility curve indicates the rate at which one good must be sacrificed to produce an additional unit of another good.

questions.text: When the demand for a good is perfectly inelastic, the price elasticity of demand is:
options: D) Less than one but greater than zero
questions.explanation: Perfectly inelastic demand means quantity demanded does not change with price, resulting in a price elasticity of demand of zero.

questions.text: A firm experiencing constant returns to scale will observe that:
options: A) Output increases at a faster rate than inputs
B) Output increases at the same rate as inputs
C) Output increases at a slower rate than inputs
D) Output remains constant with increased inputs
questions.answer: B) Output increases at the same rate as inputs
questions.explanation: Constant returns to scale occur when a proportional increase in all inputs leads to an equal proportional increase in output.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of perfect competition?
questions.explanation: In perfect competition, all firms are price takers and cannot practice price discrimination as all products are identical.

questions.text: The relationship between average cost (AC) and marginal cost (MC) can be best described as:
options: A) AC is always greater than MC
B) AC is always less than MC
C) AC intersects MC at its minimum point
D) AC and MC are unrelated
questions.answer: C) AC intersects MC at its minimum point
questions.explanation: The average cost curve intersects the marginal cost curve at the minimum point of the average cost curve.

questions.text: In the Keynesian cross model, the equilibrium level of output occurs where:
options: B) Aggregate demand equals aggregate supply
C) Marginal propensity to consume equals one
questions.answer: B) Aggregate demand equals aggregate supply
questions.explanation: Equilibrium output in the Keynesian model is determined where aggregate demand equals aggregate supply.

questions.text: The Phillips curve illustrates a relationship between:
questions.explanation: The Phillips curve shows an inverse relationship between the rate of inflation and the rate of unemployment in the short run.

questions.text: When the government increases its spending without increasing taxes, it is an example of:
questions.explanation: Increased government spending without tax increases represents expansionary fiscal policy, aimed at stimulating economic activity.

questions.text: In the circular flow of income, the leakage that does not return to firms is:
questions.explanation: Savings represent a leakage from the circular flow as they are not immediately spent on goods and services.

questions.text: Which of the following is a characteristic of a perfectly competitive market?
options: A) Few sellers dominate the market
questions.explanation: In perfect competition, all firms sell identical products, making them perfect substitutes for consumers.
questions.chapterName: Forms of Market and Price Determination

questions.text: When the price of a commodity increases by 10%, the quantity demanded decreases by 5%. The price elasticity of demand for this commodity is:
questions.explanation: Price elasticity of demand is calculated as percentage change in quantity demanded divided by percentage change in price, which equals -5%/10% = 0.5, indicating inelastic demand.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a microeconomic variable?
options: C) Price of wheat in a local market
questions.answer: C) Price of wheat in a local market
questions.explanation: Microeconomics deals with individual economic units, such as the price determination of a specific commodity like wheat.

questions.text: In the production of a good, when the marginal product of labor is negative, it means that:
options: A) Adding more workers increases output
B) Adding more workers decreases total output
C) The firm is operating at the minimum efficient scale
D) The firm is experiencing constant returns to scale
questions.answer: B) Adding more workers decreases total output
questions.explanation: A negative marginal product indicates that additional units of labor are reducing total output, likely due to overcrowding or inefficiency.
questions.chapterName: Theory of Producer Behavior and Supply

questions.text: The law of diminishing marginal utility states that:
options: A) As consumption increases, total utility decreases
B) As consumption increases, marginal utility decreases
C) As consumption increases, average utility decreases
D) As consumption increases, marginal utility increases
questions.answer: B) As consumption increases, marginal utility decreases
questions.explanation: The law states that as a consumer consumes more units of a commodity, the additional satisfaction from each successive unit tends to decrease.

questions.text: In a perfectly competitive market, the firm's demand curve is:
questions.explanation: In perfect competition, firms are price takers, meaning they can sell any quantity at the market price, resulting in a perfectly elastic (horizontal) demand curve.
questions.chapterName: Forms of Market and Price Determination

questions.text: Which of the following would NOT be considered a factor of production?
questions.explanation: Money is not a factor of production but rather a medium of exchange used to acquire factors like land, labor, and capital.

questions.text: If a firm's total cost function is TC = 100 + 5Q, where Q is output, then the firm's fixed cost is:
questions.explanation: Fixed costs are those that do not vary with output level, represented by the constant term in the total cost function.
questions.chapterName: Theory of Producer Behavior and Supply

questions.text: The cross elasticity of demand between two goods is positive. This indicates that the goods are:
questions.explanation: A positive cross elasticity indicates that the goods are substitutes, meaning an increase in the price of one leads to an increase in demand for the other.

questions.text: In the short run, a firm will continue to produce even if it incurs losses as long as:
options: A) Price is greater than average total cost
B) Price is greater than average variable cost
C) Price is greater than marginal cost
D) Price is equal to average fixed cost
questions.answer: B) Price is greater than average variable cost
questions.explanation: A firm will continue production in the short run if the price covers its variable costs, as it can minimize losses by contributing to fixed costs.
questions.chapterName: Theory of Producer Behavior and Supply

questions.text: Which of the following quantum numbers determines the orientation of an atomic orbital in space?
questions.explanation: The magnetic quantum number determines the orientation of an atomic orbital in space and can have values from -l to +l.

questions.text: Which of the following compounds will have the highest boiling point?
questions.explanation: Ethanol (CH3CH2OH) has hydrogen bonding capability, which leads to stronger intermolecular forces and higher boiling point compared to the other options.

questions.text: In the reaction: 2A + B → 3C + D, if the rate of disappearance of A is 0.5 mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹, what is the rate of appearance of C?
questions.explanation: From stoichiometry, rate of disappearance of A is 2/3 times the rate of appearance of C, so rate of appearance of C = (3/2) × 0.5 = 0.75 mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a colligative property?
options: A) Relative lowering of vapor pressure
questions.explanation: Viscosity is a physical property of the liquid itself, not a colligative property which depends on the number of solute particles.

questions.text: Which of the following has the maximum number of unpaired electrons?
questions.explanation: Mn²⁺ has 5 unpaired electrons (d⁵ configuration), while Cr³⁺ has 3, Fe²⁺ has 4, and Cu⁺ has 0 unpaired electrons.

questions.text: The standard enthalpy of formation of benzene is 49 kJ/mol. The standard enthalpy of atomization of carbon is 716 kJ/mol and that of hydrogen is 218 kJ/mol. The bond energy of C-C bond in benzene is approximately:
questions.explanation: Using the formula: ΔHf = Σ(atomization energies) - Σ(bond energies), and considering benzene has 6 C-H bonds and 3 C-C bonds, we calculate the bond energy.

questions.text: Which of the following compounds will undergo SN1 reaction most readily?
questions.explanation: Tertiary alkyl halides undergo SN1 reactions most readily due to the stability of the tertiary carbocation intermediate formed during the reaction.

questions.text: The half-life of a first-order reaction is 30 minutes. What percentage of the reaction will be completed in 60 minutes?
questions.explanation: For a first-order reaction, after two half-lives (60 minutes), 75% of the reactant will have been converted to product.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about molecular orbitals is incorrect?
options: A) Bonding molecular orbitals have lower energy than the atomic orbitals from which they are formed.
B) Antibonding molecular orbitals have higher energy than the atomic orbitals from which they are formed.
C) The number of molecular orbitals formed equals the number of atomic orbitals combined.
D) Electrons are filled in molecular orbitals in the order of increasing energy, but always with parallel spins first.
questions.answer: D) Electrons are filled in molecular orbitals in the order of increasing energy, but always with parallel spins first.
questions.explanation: Electrons are filled in molecular orbitals following Hund's rule (parallel spins first) only when orbitals of equal energy are available, not universally.

questions.text: Which of the following represents the correct order of acidic strength?
questions.explanation: For oxyacids, acid strength increases with the number of oxygen atoms attached to the central atom, so perchloric acid is the strongest and hypochlorous acid is the weakest.

questions.text: Which of the following quantum numbers determines the orientation of an atomic orbital?
questions.explanation: The magnetic quantum number determines the orientation of an atomic orbital in space.

questions.text: In which of the following processes is the entropy of the system expected to decrease?
questions.explanation: Freezing of water is a process where liquid water transitions to solid ice, resulting in a more ordered state and decreased entropy.

questions.text: Which of the following has the highest electronegativity?
questions.explanation: Fluorine has the highest electronegativity among all elements due to its small atomic size and high effective nuclear charge.

questions.text: The rate of a reaction doubles when the concentration of reactant is doubled. The order of the reaction is:
questions.explanation: In a first-order reaction, the rate is directly proportional to the concentration of the reactant, hence doubling concentration doubles the rate.

questions.text: Which of the following ions has a square planar geometry?
questions.explanation: Pt²⁺ forms square planar complexes due to its large size and high charge density, resulting in strong crystal field splitting.

questions.text: The boiling point of which of the following compounds is highest?
questions.explanation: Ethanol (CH₃CH₂OH) has the highest boiling point due to hydrogen bonding, which requires more energy to break.
questions.chapterName: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text: Which of the following elements has the highest ionization energy?
questions.explanation: Magnesium has a higher ionization energy than sodium due to its smaller atomic size and stable half-filled p-subshell configuration.

questions.text: The hybridization of carbon in diamond is:
questions.explanation: In diamond, each carbon atom is tetrahedrally bonded to four other carbon atoms, requiring sp³ hybridization.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is true for a spontaneous process?
questions.explanation: For a spontaneous process, the Gibbs free energy change (ΔG) must be negative, indicating the process can occur without external intervention.

questions.text: The complex [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ is paramagnetic. The number of unpaired electrons in it is:
questions.explanation: [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ has Co³⁺ with d⁶ configuration and strong field ligands, resulting in three unpaired electrons in the t₂g orbitals.

questions.text: Which of the following organelles is known as the 'suicide bag' of the cell?
questions.explanation: Lysosomes contain digestive enzymes that can break down cellular waste and even digest the cell itself during programmed cell death.

questions.text: During which stage of meiosis does crossing over occur?
questions.explanation: Crossing over occurs during prophase I of meiosis when homologous chromosomes exchange genetic material, creating genetic diversity.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of meristematic tissue?
questions.explanation: Meristematic cells have dense cytoplasm, small size, and thin cell walls but lack large vacuoles as they are metabolically active.

questions.text: The enzyme that catalyzes the first step of Calvin cycle is:
questions.explanation: Ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase (RuBisCO) catalyzes the fixation of CO2 to RuBP in the first step of Calvin cycle.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a coenzyme?
questions.explanation: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) is a coenzyme that acts as an electron carrier in various metabolic reactions.

questions.text: The movement of water through a semi-permeable membrane due to difference in solute concentration is called:
questions.explanation: Osmosis is the specific movement of solvent molecules (usually water) through a selectively permeable membrane from low to high solute concentration.

questions.text: Which of the following blood vessels has the thickest wall?
questions.explanation: Arteries have thicker walls than veins to withstand the high pressure of blood pumped directly from the heart.

questions.text: The process by which a gene alters its expression in response to environmental factors without changing the DNA sequence is known as:
questions.explanation: Epigenetic modifications alter gene expression without changing the DNA sequence, often through DNA methylation or histone modification.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a function of the liver?
options: C) Production of red blood cells
questions.answer: C) Production of red blood cells
questions.explanation: While the liver performs many functions, including glycogen storage, detoxification, and bile secretion, red blood cell production occurs primarily in bone marrow.

questions.text: The hormone that regulates calcium levels in the blood by promoting calcium reabsorption in the kidneys is:
questions.explanation: Parathyroid hormone increases blood calcium levels by stimulating calcium reabsorption in the kidneys and bone resorption.

questions.text: Which of the following is a characteristic of a federal form of government?
options: A) Power is concentrated in the central government
B) Power is divided between the central and state governments
C) States have more power than the central government
D) Local governments have supreme authority
questions.answer: B) Power is divided between the central and state governments
questions.explanation: Federalism involves the sharing of power between a central/national government and regional state governments.

questions.text: The 'Green Revolution' in India primarily introduced which of the following to increase agricultural productivity?
questions.explanation: The Green Revolution focused on the introduction of high-yielding variety seeds, chemical fertilizers, and pesticides to increase agricultural output.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental right guaranteed by the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Right to Property was originally a fundamental right but was removed by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978.

questions.text: The 'Doctrine of Lapse' was introduced by which British Governor-General?
questions.explanation: Lord Dalhousie introduced the Doctrine of Lapse, which allowed the British to annex princely states if a ruler died without a male heir.

questions.text: Which of the following is a primary function of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)?
options: A) To provide loans directly to individuals
B) To print and manage currency in India
D) To control foreign exchange only
questions.answer: B) To print and manage currency in India
questions.explanation: The RBI is the central bank of India and has the authority to print and manage the country's currency supply.

questions.text: The 'Chipko Movement' was primarily associated with the protection of which natural resource?
questions.explanation: The Chipko Movement was an environmental movement aimed at protecting forests from deforestation through non-violent means.

questions.text: Which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution abolishes untouchability?
questions.explanation: Article 17 of the Indian Constitution explicitly abolishes the practice of untouchability and its practice in any form is forbidden.

questions.text: The 'Dandi March' was organized by Mahatma Gandhi primarily to protest against which British policy?
questions.explanation: The Dandi March (1930) was a non-violent protest against the British salt monopoly, which forced Indians to pay salt tax.

questions.text: Which of the following is a feature of a democratic form of government?
questions.explanation: Free and fair elections are a cornerstone of democracy, allowing citizens to choose their representatives through voting.

questions.text: The 'White Revolution' in India, also known as 'Operation Flood', was primarily associated with which sector?
questions.explanation: Operation Flood, launched in 1970, was a dairy development program that made India the world's largest milk producer.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of ionic compounds?
options: A) High melting and boiling points
C) Conduct electricity in solid state
questions.answer: C) Conduct electricity in solid state
questions.explanation: Ionic compounds do not conduct electricity in solid state as their ions are fixed in position, but they do conduct when molten or dissolved in water.

questions.text: The process by which plants lose water vapour through tiny pores on their leaves is called:
