questions.explanation: Transpiration is the biological process where water vapour is released from plant leaves through stomata, helping in water movement and temperature regulation.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a renewable source of energy?
questions.explanation: Natural gas is a fossil fuel and takes millions of years to form, making it non-renewable, unlike solar, wind, and biomass which can be replenished naturally.

questions.text: When an object is placed between the focus and optical center of a convex lens, the image formed is:
questions.explanation: When an object is placed between the focus and optical center of a convex lens, a virtual, erect, and magnified image is formed on the same side as the object.

questions.text: Which of the following metals will NOT displace hydrogen from dilute hydrochloric acid?
questions.explanation: Copper is less reactive than hydrogen and cannot displace hydrogen from dilute acids, unlike magnesium, aluminum, and zinc which are more reactive.

questions.text: The hormone that regulates blood sugar levels by promoting glucose uptake by cells is:
questions.explanation: Insulin is produced by the pancreas and helps lower blood glucose levels by facilitating its uptake into cells for energy production or storage.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a greenhouse gas?
questions.explanation: Oxygen is not a greenhouse gas as it does not significantly absorb and re-emit infrared radiation that contributes to the greenhouse effect.

questions.text: In the given electrical circuit, if the resistance of R1 is 2Ω and R2 is 3Ω, and they are connected in parallel, the equivalent resistance is:
questions.explanation: For parallel resistors, the equivalent resistance is calculated as 1/R = 1/R1 + 1/R2, which gives 1/R = 1/2 + 1/3 = 5/6, so R = 6/5 = 1.2Ω.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about DNA is incorrect?
options: B) It is a double-stranded helix
C) It is found in the cytoplasm of prokaryotes
D) Its basic unit is nucleotide
questions.answer: C) It is found in the cytoplasm of prokaryotes
questions.explanation: In prokaryotes, DNA is found in the nucleoid region, which is not the cytoplasm, and it lacks a nuclear membrane unlike eukaryotes.

questions.text: A 2kg object is moving with a velocity of 5m/s. If the velocity is doubled, the kinetic energy of the object will:
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy is proportional to the square of velocity (KE = ½mv²), so when velocity doubles, kinetic energy becomes four times the original value.

questions.text: The sum of two numbers is 27 and their product is 182. What are the numbers?
questions.explanation: Let the numbers be x and y. Then x + y = 27 and xy = 182. Solving these equations gives x = 13 and y = 14.

questions.text: If the HCF of 120 and 144 is 24, then the LCM is:
questions.explanation: For any two numbers, HCF × LCM = Product of the numbers. So, LCM = (120 × 144) ÷ 24 = 720.

questions.text: A circle has a radius of 14 cm. The area of the sector formed by a central angle of 60° is:
If the arithmetic mean of 6, 8, 10, x, 12 is 10, then the value of x is:
questions.explanation: Mean = (6 + 8 + 10 + x + 12)/5 = 10. Solving gives x = 14.

questions.text: The value of sin²30° + cos²60° is:
If a line segment AB is divided by a point P in the ratio 2:3, and AB = 10 cm, then AP is:
questions.explanation: AP/PB = 2/3 and AP + PB = 10 cm. Solving gives AP = 4 cm.

questions.text: The sum of the first 15 terms of an arithmetic progression with first term 3 and common difference 4 is:
If tanθ = 3/4, then the value of sinθ is:
questions.explanation: If tanθ = 3/4, then in a right triangle, opposite side = 3, adjacent side = 4, so hypotenuse = 5. Thus sinθ = opposite/hypotenuse = 3/5.

questions.text: A metallic sphere of radius 4.2 cm is melted and recast into the shape of a cylinder of radius 6 cm. The height of the cylinder is:
questions.explanation: Volume of sphere = 4/3 × π × 4.2³ = Volume of cylinder = π × 6² × h. Solving gives h = 2.45 cm.

questions.text: The probability that a leap year selected at random will contain 53 Sundays is:
questions.explanation: A leap year has 366 days = 52 weeks + 2 days. These 2 days can be any of the 7 pairs of days, and 2 of these pairs include a Sunday. So probability = 2/7.

questions.text: किस विशेषता के कारण 'मेरा प्यारा भारत' कविता को गीत का दर्जा प्राप्त है?
questions.explanation: यह कविता गीत के रूप में गाई जा सकती है, जिसके लिए गुण गायन की संभावना एक महत्वपूर्ण तत्व है।

questions.text: किस प्रकार का अलंकार 'चाँद जैसा चेहरा' में प्रयुक्त है?
questions.explanation: यहाँ चेहरे की सुंदरता को चाँद से तुलना करके उपमा अलंकार का प्रयोग किया गया है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा वाक्य 'विशेषण' का उदाहरण नहीं है?
options: A) वह एक बुद्धिमान व्यक्ति है।
D) वह बहुत अच्छा गाता है।
questions.explanation: यहाँ 'वह किताब पढ़ता है' में कोई विशेषण नहीं है, जबकि अन्य वाक्यों में विशेषण उपस्थित हैं।

questions.text: 'दूर गगन से चमक उठा सा' पंक्ति में किस अलंकार का प्रयोग किया गया है?
questions.explanation: यहाँ चमक को गगन से उठता हुआ बताकर उत्प्रेक्षा अलंकार का प्रयोग किया गया है।

questions.text: किस लेखक ने 'मेरा प्यारा भारत' लिखा है?
questions.explanation: 'मेरा प्यारा भारत' कविता सुभद्रा कुमारी चौहान द्वारा लिखी गई है।

questions.text: अनेकार्थक शब्द का उदाहरण क्या है?
questions.explanation: 'घर' शब्द के अनेक अर्थ हो सकते हैं - आवास, परिवार, वंश आदि, इसलिए यह अनेकार्थक शब्द है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा 'विशेषण' का उदाहरण नहीं है?
questions.explanation: 'चलता' क्रिया है, जबकि 'सुंदर', 'तेज़' और 'बड़ा' विशेषण हैं।

questions.text: 'जब तक जीवन है, तब तक कर्म है' यह विचार किस साहित्यकार का है?
questions.explanation: यह विचार स्वामी विवेकानंद का है, जिन्होंने कर्म योग पर बल दिया था।

questions.text: 'नीलकंठ' उपन्यास किस लेखक की रचना है?
questions.explanation: 'नीलकंठ' उपन्यास आचार्य चतुरसेन द्वारा लिखा गया है।

questions.text: किस अलंकार का प्रयोग 'राजा हरिश्चंद्र' में हुआ है?
questions.explanation: 'राजा हरिश्चंद्र' की कथा में श्लेष अलंकार का प्रयोग किया गया है, जहाँ शब्दों के अर्थों का खेल होता है।

questions.text: किस विशेषता से 'देशभक्ति' की भावना का प्रभावी ढंग से व्यक्त होता है?
options: A) अपने देश की तुलना दूसरे देशों से करना
B) देश के लिए कुछ भी त्याग करने की तैयारी रखना
D) देश के इतिहास को भूल जाना
questions.answer: B) देश के लिए कुछ भी त्याग करने की तैयारी रखना
questions.explanation: देशभक्ति का सबसे महत्वपूर्ण पहलू देश के लिए त्याग करने की भावना है, जो देश की सेवा में अपने सुख-सुविधाओं को पीछे छोड़ने को दर्शाता है।

questions.text: हिंदी साहित्य में 'छायावाद' कब और कहाँ उभरा?
options: A) 19वीं सदी के उत्तरार्ध में बंगाल में
B) 20वीं सदी के पूर्वार्ध में मध्य प्रदेश में
C) 20वीं सदी के मध्य में उत्तर प्रदेश में
D) 18वीं सदी के अंत में दिल्ली में
questions.answer: A) 19वीं सदी के उत्तरार्ध में बंगाल में
questions.explanation: छायावाद का उदय 19वीं सदी के उत्तरार्ध में बंगाल में हुआ और यह आधुनिक हिंदी काव्य की पहली बड़ी धारा बनी।

questions.text: 'अनुप्रास' अलंकार का उदाहरण कौन सा है?
options: D) सुनो भाई, सुनो मेरी बात
questions.explanation: अनुप्रास अलंकार में एक ही वर्ण या ध्वनि का बार-बार प्रयोग किया जाता है, जैसे 'प्रिय बिहारी, प्यारे बिहारी' में 'ब' वर्ण का अनुप्रास है।

questions.text: महात्मा गांधी द्वारा 'अहिंसा' के सिद्धांत का सबसे उचित व्याख्या क्या है?
options: A) शत्रु के सामने हाथ न उठाना
B) मन से भी किसी को कष्ट न देना
questions.answer: B) मन से भी किसी को कष्ट न देना
questions.explanation: गांधीजी के अनुसार अहिंसा केवल शारीरिक हिंसा से बचना ही नहीं, बल्कि मन से भी किसी को कष्ट न देना और प्रेम से प्रतिक्रिया करना है।

questions.text: हिंदी में 'वाक्य' किसे कहते हैं?
options: A) किसी एक शब्द का प्रयोग
B) एक से अधिक शब्दों का समूह जिसका पूर्ण अर्थ हो
questions.answer: B) एक से अधिक शब्दों का समूह जिसका पूर्ण अर्थ हो
questions.explanation: वाक्य एक से अधिक शब्दों का ऐसा समूह होता है जिसका कोई पूर्ण अर्थ और अंतिम बिंदु होता है।

questions.text: 'उपमा' अलंकार में क्या विशेषता होती है?
options: A) दो वस्तुओं की तुलना में 'जैसा' शब्द का प्रयोग
B) दो वस्तुओं की तुलना में 'सा' शब्द का प्रयोग
C) दो वस्तुओं की तुलना में 'जैसे' शब्द का प्रयोग
D) दो वस्तुओं की तुलना में 'भी' शब्द का प्रयोग
questions.answer: B) दो वस्तुओं की तुलना में 'सा' शब्द का प्रयोग
questions.explanation: उपमा अलंकार में दो वस्तुओं की तुलना करते समय 'सा' शब्द का प्रयोग किया जाता है, जैसे 'नेता सा चेहरा'।

questions.text: हिंदी के प्रथम उपन्यास के रूप में कौन सा ग्रंथ माना जाता है?
questions.explanation: देवकीनंदन खत्री द्वारा लिखित 'चंद्रकांता' को हिंदी का पहला उपन्यास माना जाता है, जिसने हिंदी उपन्यास लेखन को नई दिशा दी।

questions.text: 'रस' किसे कहा जाता है?
questions.explanation: रस काव्य की वह भावनात्मक अभिव्यंजकता है जो पाठक के मन पर गहरा प्रभाव डालती है।

questions.text: हिंदी में 'विशेषण' क्या होता है?
options: A) क्रिया को बताने वाला शब्द
B) व्यक्ति या वस्तु के गुण को बताने वाला शब्द
C) संज्ञा को बताने वाला शब्द
D) क्रिया के समय को बताने वाला शब्द
questions.answer: B) व्यक्ति या वस्तु के गुण को बताने वाला शब्द
questions.explanation: विशेषण वह शब्द होता है जो किसी व्यक्ति, वस्तु या गुण का वर्णन करता है, जैसे 'सुंदर फूल' में 'सुंदर' विशेषण है।

questions.text: हिंदी में 'अनुनासिक' वर्ण किसे कहा जाता है?
options: A) नासिका से निकलने वाले वर्ण
B) मुँह से निकलने वाले वर्ण
C) जीभ के मध्य भाग से निकलने वाले वर्ण
D) होठों से निकलने वाले वर्ण
questions.answer: A) नासिका से निकलने वाले वर्ण
questions.explanation: अनुनासिक वर्ण वे वर्ण होते हैं जो नासिका से निकलते हैं, जैसे ङ, ञ, ण, न, म, ँ।

questions.text: In the sentence 'The book belongs to me,' which word is a possessive pronoun?
questions.explanation: 'Me' is a possessive pronoun as it indicates ownership of the book.

questions.text: Identify the figure of speech in: 'The wind whispered secrets through the trees.'
questions.explanation: The wind is given human quality of whispering, making it personification.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a transitive verb?
questions.explanation: 'Eat' is transitive as it requires an object (what is being eaten).

questions.text: In the sentence 'She is taller than her sister,' what type of comparison is used?
questions.explanation: The sentence compares two entities using 'than', indicating a comparative degree.

questions.text: Which of the following sentences uses the passive voice correctly?
options: A) The cat chased the mouse.
B) The mouse was chased by the cat.
C) The cat is chasing the mouse.
D) The mouse chases the cat.
questions.answer: B) The mouse was chased by the cat.
questions.explanation: Passive voice emphasizes the receiver of the action and uses 'by' to indicate the doer.

questions.text: Identify the correct form of the verb in the conditional sentence: 'If I _____ you, I would study harder.'
questions.explanation: In unreal conditional sentences, 'were' is used with all subjects, including 'I'.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of an idiom?
questions.explanation: 'Break a leg' is an idiom meaning good luck, though literally it means something unfortunate.

questions.text: In the sentence 'The children played happily in the garden,' what part of speech is 'happily'?
questions.explanation: 'Happily' describes how the children played, making it an adverb modifying the verb.

questions.text: Which of the following sentences contains a misplaced modifier?
options: A) The teacher gave the students an interesting assignment.
B) The students who studied hard passed the exam.
C) Running quickly, the dog caught the ball.
D) The dog with the long tail chased the cat across the street.
questions.answer: C) Running quickly, the dog caught the ball.
questions.explanation: The modifier 'running quickly' could ambiguously modify either the dog or the ball.

questions.text: Identify the type of conjunction in: 'He wanted to go, but it was raining.'
questions.explanation: 'But' is a coordinating conjunction as it connects two independent clauses of equal importance.

questions.text: Identify the figure of speech in the following line: 'The wind stood up and gave a shout.'
questions.explanation: The wind is given human qualities of standing up and shouting, which is personification.

questions.text: Which of the following sentences is correctly punctuated?
options: A) 'Please bring me, a cup of coffee.'
B) 'Please bring me a cup of coffee.'
C) 'Please bring me a cup of coffee', she said.
D) 'Please bring me a cup of coffee,' she said.
questions.answer: D) 'Please bring me a cup of coffee,' she said.
questions.explanation: Option D correctly places the comma after the direct address and before the reporting verb.

questions.text: What is the antonym of 'Eloquent'?
questions.explanation: Inarticulate means unable to express ideas fluently or coherently, which is the opposite of eloquent.

questions.text: In the sentence 'The committee has submitted its report,' the underlined word is:
questions.explanation: Committee is a collective noun as it refers to a group of people considered as a single unit.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a palindrome?
questions.explanation: A palindrome is a word that reads the same backward as forward, like 'level'.

questions.text: Identify the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence: 'The teacher praised the student.'
options: A) The student was praised by the teacher.
B) The student is praised by the teacher.
C) The student praised by the teacher.
D) The student has been praised by the teacher.
questions.answer: A) The student was praised by the teacher.
questions.explanation: The passive voice construction requires the appropriate form of 'be' verb (was) before the past participle (praised).

questions.text: What is the meaning of the idiom 'To bite the bullet'?
options: B) To face a difficult situation with courage
questions.answer: B) To face a difficult situation with courage
questions.explanation: The idiom 'to bite the bullet' means to endure a painful or difficult situation bravely.

questions.text: Which of the following sentences correctly uses the subjunctive mood?
options: A) If I was you, I would study harder.
B) If I were you, I would study harder.
C) If I am you, I would study harder.
D) If I will be you, I would study harder.
questions.answer: B) If I were you, I would study harder.
questions.explanation: The subjunctive mood is used for hypothetical situations, and 'were' is the correct form after 'if' for all subjects.

questions.text: In the sentence 'Ravi is taller than any other boy in his class,' the figure of speech used is:
questions.explanation: The statement is an exaggeration as Ravi cannot be taller than himself, making it an example of hyperbole.

questions.text: Which of the following words is an example of onomatopoeia?
questions.explanation: Onomatopoeia is a word that phonetically imitates the sound it describes, like 'buzz' for the sound of a bee.

questions.text: Which of the following factors contributed most to the decline of the Indian handloom industry in the 19th century?
options: A) Introduction of power looms in Britain
B) Increase in demand for handwoven textiles
C) Government support for Indian weavers
D) Decline in cotton production in India
questions.answer: A) Introduction of power looms in Britain
questions.explanation: The introduction of power looms in Britain made machine-made textiles cheaper and more abundant, leading to a decline in demand for Indian handloom products.

questions.text: In the context of the French Revolution, which estate had to bear the maximum burden of taxation?
options: D) The King and his immediate family
questions.explanation: The Third Estate, comprising commoners, peasants, and the urban poor, bore the heaviest tax burden while enjoying few privileges compared to the clergy and nobility.

questions.text: Which of the following rivers flows through a rift valley?
questions.explanation: The Narmada river flows through a rift valley between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges, making it unique among major Indian rivers.

questions.text: What was the primary objective of the 'Rowlatt Act' passed by the British government in India in 1919?
options: A) To extend the period of detention without trial
C) To reform the educational system
D) To increase representation of Indians in the legislature
questions.answer: A) To extend the period of detention without trial
questions.explanation: The Rowlatt Act allowed the British government to imprison Indians without trial, which was strongly opposed by Indian leaders like Gandhi.

questions.text: Which of the following factors is most responsible for the monsoon climate of India?
options: B) Differential heating of land and water
questions.answer: B) Differential heating of land and water
questions.explanation: The monsoon climate of India is primarily caused by the differential heating of the Indian subcontinent and the surrounding oceans, creating pressure differences.

questions.text: In the context of the Russian Revolution, what was the 'April Theses'?
options: A) A proposal to establish a constitutional monarchy
B) A set of revolutionary demands by Lenin
C) A plan for economic reforms
D) An agreement with Germany to end World War I
questions.answer: B) A set of revolutionary demands by Lenin
questions.explanation: The April Theses were a series of ten directives issued by Lenin in 1917, calling for Soviet control of the state and an end to the provisional government.
questions.chapterName: Socialism in Europe and the Russian Revolution

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the parliamentary system of government in India?
options: A) Executive responsible to the legislature
C) Prime Minister as the head of government
D) President as the ceremonial head of state
questions.explanation: India follows a parliamentary system with fusion of powers rather than strict separation, where the executive is drawn from and responsible to the legislature.

questions.text: What was the main purpose of the 'Simon Commission' sent to India in 1928?
options: A) To assess the progress of civil disobedience movement
B) To study constitutional reforms for India
C) To review the economic conditions of India
D) To investigate the Jallianwala Bagh incident
questions.answer: B) To study constitutional reforms for India
questions.explanation: The Simon Commission was sent to India to discuss and recommend constitutional reforms, but it had no Indian members, which led to its boycott.

questions.text: Which of the following is a characteristic of the 'Later Vedic Period'?
questions.explanation: The Later Vedic Period saw the emergence and strengthening of the varna system, with Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, and Shudras becoming more defined.

questions.text: What was the primary reason for the decline of the Indus Valley Civilization?
options: B) Deforestation and drying up of rivers
questions.answer: B) Deforestation and drying up of rivers
questions.explanation: The decline of the Indus Valley Civilization is attributed to environmental factors including deforestation, drying up of the Saraswati river, and changing climatic conditions.

questions.text: Which of the following factors contributed most to the decline of the Mughal Empire in the 18th century?
options: B) The rise of regional kingdoms
D) Economic challenges due to long wars
questions.explanation: The decline accelerated after Aurangzeb's death in 1707 as his successors lacked his administrative abilities and faced numerous rebellions.

questions.text: Which constitutional amendment in India reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 years?
questions.explanation: The 61st Amendment Act of 1988 lowered the voting age from 21 to 18 years, expanding democratic participation among youth.

questions.text: Which of the following rivers is known as the 'Dakshin Ganga'?
questions.explanation: The Godavari River is called the 'Dakshin Ganga' due to its length and significance in peninsular India, similar to the Ganga in the north.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental right under the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Right to Property was originally a fundamental right but was removed by the 44th Amendment Act in 1978 and made a legal right.

questions.text: Which of the following factors primarily led to the partition of India in 1947?
questions.explanation: The Two-Nation Theory, advocated by the Muslim League, posited that Hindus and Muslims were separate nations, forming the ideological basis for partition.

questions.text: Which of the following is the main reason for the high population density in the Northern Plains of India?
options: B) Fertile soil and agricultural productivity
questions.answer: B) Fertile soil and agricultural productivity
questions.explanation: The Northern Plains have alluvial soil, perennial rivers, and suitable climate for agriculture, supporting high population density for centuries.

questions.text: Which of the following movements was primarily led by Mahatma Gandhi against the British salt tax?
questions.explanation: The Salt March (1930) was a key event of the Civil Disobedience Movement, where Gandhi violated the salt tax to protest British economic policies.

questions.text: Which of the following factors contributes most to the uneven distribution of population in India?
questions.explanation: The uneven distribution of population in India results from a combination of historical settlements, topographical features, and climatic conditions.

questions.text: Which of the following was the main objective of the Panchayati Raj system introduced in India?
options: B) Decentralizing administration and promoting local self-governance
questions.answer: B) Decentralizing administration and promoting local self-governance
questions.explanation: The Panchayati Raj system aims to democratize governance by empowering local communities to make decisions about their development.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the Himalayan rivers is correct?
options: A) They are perennial due to glacial and rainwater
D) They have smaller drainage basins
questions.answer: A) They are perennial due to glacial and rainwater
questions.explanation: Himalayan rivers are perennial because they are fed by both melting glaciers and monsoon rains, ensuring water flow throughout the year.

questions.text: Which of the following is the correct formula for calculating the speed of an object?
questions.explanation: Speed is defined as the distance traveled per unit of time, so it is calculated by dividing the distance by the time taken.

questions.text: When an object is immersed in a fluid, it experiences an upward force equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by it. This statement is known as:
options: A) Newton's first law of motion
questions.explanation: Archimedes' principle states that the buoyant force on an object immersed in a fluid is equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by the object.

questions.text: Which of the following elements is a metalloid?
questions.explanation: Silicon is a metalloid, exhibiting properties intermediate between metals and non-metals, such as being a semiconductor.

questions.text: The process by which green plants prepare their own food using sunlight is called:
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water to produce glucose and oxygen.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a true solution?
options: B) The solute particles cannot be seen
C) The solute particles settle down over time
D) It cannot be separated by filtration
questions.answer: C) The solute particles settle down over time
questions.explanation: In a true solution, the solute particles are uniformly distributed and do not settle down over time, which is a characteristic of a suspension.

questions.text: The acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the Earth is approximately:
questions.explanation: The acceleration due to gravity on Earth's surface is approximately 9.8 m/s², which is the value used in most physics calculations.

questions.text: Which of the following organelles is known as the 'powerhouse of the cell'?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are called the 'powerhouse of the cell' because they produce ATP, the energy currency of the cell, through cellular respiration.

questions.text: When a ray of light passes from air to water, it undergoes:
questions.explanation: When light passes from one medium to another, it both refracts (changes direction) and reflects (bounces back partially) at the interface.

questions.text: Which of the following is a chemical change?
questions.explanation: Burning of paper is a chemical change as it involves the formation of new substances with different properties, unlike the physical changes listed in other options.

questions.text: The force required to keep an object moving in a circular path at constant speed is called:
questions.explanation: Centripetal force is the inward force that keeps an object moving in a circular path at constant speed, directed towards the center of the circle.

questions.text: The sum of three consecutive even integers is 42. What is the smallest of these integers?
questions.explanation: Let the integers be x, x+2, x+4. Then x + (x+2) + (x+4) = 42, which gives x = 12.

questions.text: In a triangle ABC, if ∠A = 50° and ∠B = 70°, then the measure of ∠C is:
questions.explanation: The sum of angles in a triangle is 180°, so ∠C = 180° - 50° - 70° = 60°.

questions.text: The value of (2√3 + √5)(2√3 - √5) is:
questions.explanation: This is in the form (a+b)(a-b) = a² - b², so (2√3)² - (√5)² = 12 - 5 = 7.

questions.text: If a polynomial p(x) is divided by (x - 2), the remainder is 5. If p(x) is divided by (x - 3), the remainder is 7. What is the remainder when p(x) is divided by (x - 2)(x - 3)?
questions.explanation: Using Remainder Theorem, when p(x) is divided by (x-2)(x-3), the remainder is linear: ax + b. Substituting x=2 gives 2a + b = 5, and x=3 gives 3a + b = 7. Solving these gives a=2, b=-1.

questions.text: A cylinder has height 10 cm and radius 3 cm. What is its volume in cubic cm?
questions.explanation: Volume of cylinder = πr²h = π × 3² × 10 = 90π cubic cm.

questions.text: If the mean of the numbers 3, 5, 7, x, 11 is 7, then the value of x is:
In a right triangle ABC, right-angled at B, if AB = 6 cm and BC = 8 cm, then the length of AC is:
questions.explanation: Using Pythagoras theorem, AC² = AB² + BC² = 6² + 8² = 36 + 64 = 100, so AC = 10 cm.

questions.text: The value of sin²30° + cos²60° is:
If a line makes angles of 45°, 60°, and 90° with the x, y, and z-axes respectively, then the direction cosines of the line are:
questions.explanation: Direction cosines are (cosα, cosβ, cosγ) where α, β, γ are angles with x, y, z axes respectively. So (cos45°, cos60°, cos90°) = (1/√2, 1/2, 0).

questions.text: A bag contains 5 red balls and 3 blue balls. If one ball is drawn at random, the probability that it is red is:
questions.explanation: Total balls = 5 + 3 = 8. Probability of drawing red ball = number of red balls / total balls = 5/8.

questions.text: किस विशेषता के कारण 'बिहारी' की बैठक रीतिकालीन काव्य की प्रमुख बैठक मानी जाती है?
questions.explanation: बिहारी ने अपनी रचनाओं में विभिन्न प्रकार की नायिकाओं का विशद वर्णन किया है, जो उन्हें बैठक रीति का प्रमुख कवि बनाता है।

questions.text: हिंदी भाषा का सर्वप्रथम उपन्यास कौन सा माना जाता है?
questions.explanation: भारतेन्दु हरिश्चंद्र द्वारा रचित 'अलघ रास' को हिंदी का पहला उपन्यास माना जाता है, जो 1882 में प्रकाशित हुआ था।

questions.text: कवि 'सूर' की कौन सी रचना मुगल बादशाह अकबर के दरबार में प्रसिद्ध थी?
questions.explanation: सूरदास की 'अमीर हम्जा' नामक रचना अकबर के दरबार में बहुत प्रसिद्ध थी और उन्हें 'सूर' के नाम से जाना जाने लगा।

questions.text: आधुनिक हिंदी कविता के 'प्रयोगवाद' का प्रमुख प्रवर्तक कौन था?
questions.explanation: सुमित्रानंदन पंत को हिंदी कविता में प्रयोगवाद का प्रमुख प्रवर्तक माना जाता है, जिन्होंने छंदों और भाषा में नई प्रयोगों को प्रोत्साहित किया।

questions.text: भारतेन्दु हरिश्चंद्र का नाटक 'विद्या सुंदर' का मुख्य विषय क्या है?
questions.explanation: भारतेन्दु का नाटक 'विद्या सुंदर' सामाजीय सुधारों और शिक्षा के महत्व पर केंद्रित है, जो उनकी सामाजिक चेतना का प्रतीक है।

questions.text: महादेवी वर्मा की कौन सी कृति 'नीरजा' के नाम से प्रसिद्ध है?
questions.explanation: महादेवी वर्मा का 'नीरजा' उनका प्रसिद्ध कविता संग्रह है, जिसमें उनकी गहरी भावनात्मक कविताएं संकलित हैं।

questions.text: गुलाब राय वर्मा की प्रसिद्ध रचना 'आमा' का मुख्य विषय क्या है?
questions.explanation: गुलाब राय वर्मा की 'आमा' मातृ प्रेम और माता के स्नेह का गहरा वर्णन करती है, जो उनकी सर्वोत्तम रचनाओं में से एक है।

questions.text: आचार्य रामचंद्र शुक्ल द्वारा रचित 'हिंदी साहित्य का इतिहास' में किस युग को 'आदिकाल' कहा गया है?
questions.explanation: आचार्य रामचंद्र शुक्ल ने अपने 'हिंदी साहित्य का इतिहास' में वैदिक काल को 'आदिकाल' के रूप में संदर्भित किया है।

questions.text: जयशंकर प्रसाद के नाटक 'स्कंद गुप्त' में किस ऐतिहासिक व्यक्ति का चित्रण है?
questions.explanation: जयशंकर प्रसाद के नाटक 'स्कंद गुप्त' में गुप्त वंश के प्रसिद्ध सम्राट समुद्रगुप्त का चित्रण है।

questions.text: कवि 'मिर्जा गालिब' की कौन सी रचना उर्दू और हिंदी दोनों भाषाओं में प्रसिद्ध है?
questions.explanation: मिर्जा गालिब की 'ग़ालिब शायरी' उनकी सर्वाधिक प्रसिद्ध रचना है, जो उर्दू और हिंदी दोनों भाषाओं में प्रभावशाली रही है।

questions.text: विशेषण का क्या कार्य होता है?
questions.explanation: विशेषण शब्द किसी संज्ञा या प्रदर्शन शब्द की विशेषता या गुण को दर्शाते हैं।

questions.text: 'गीता' शब्द का विशेषण क्या होगा?
questions.explanation: 'गीता' शब्द का विशेषण 'गीतिक' होगा, क्योंकि यह गीत से संबंधित है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा वाक्य सही है?
options: A) वह बहुत अच्छा लड़का है
B) वह बहुत अच्छा लड़का था
C) वह बहुत अच्छा लड़का होगा
D) वह बहुत अच्छा लड़का हैगा
questions.answer: A) वह बहुत अच्छा लड़का है
questions.explanation: वाक्य 'वह बहुत अच्छा लड़का है' सही है, क्योंकि इसमें वर्तमाकाल का प्रयोग है और विशेषण 'बहुत' का उपयोग उचित है।

questions.text: 'बादल' शब्द का विशेषण क्या होगा?
questions.explanation: 'बादल' शब्द का विशेषण 'बादलिक' होगा, जो बादल से संबंधित होता है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा शब्द 'विशेषण' नहीं है?
questions.explanation: 'दौड़ना' एक क्रिया है, जबकि 'सुंदर', 'तेज़' और 'बड़ा' विशेषण हैं।

questions.text: 'वह बहुत तेज़ दौड़ता है' में 'तेज़' क्या है?
questions.explanation: 'तेज़' शब्द 'दौड़ना' की गति की विशेषता बता रहा है, इसलिए यह संज्ञा विशेषण है।

questions.text: विशेषण कितन प्रकार के होते हैं?
questions.explanation: विशेषण चार प्रकार के होते हैं: गुणवाचक, विशेषण, संख्यावाचक और परिमाणवाचक।

questions.text: 'प्रत्येक व्यक्ति को अपने-अपने कर्तव्यों का पालन करना चाहिए' में 'प्रत्येक' क्या है?
questions.explanation: 'प्रत्येक' शब्द 'व्यक्ति' की विशेषता बता रहा है, इसलिए यह विशेषण है।

questions.text: 'वह बहुत बुरा काम करता है' में 'बहुत' क्या है?
questions.explanation: 'बहुत' शब्द 'बुरा' की मात्रा या परिमाण बता रहा है, इसलिए यह परिमाणवाचक विशेषण है।

questions.text: 'राम अपनी माँ को प्यार करता है' में 'अपनी' क्या है?
questions.explanation: 'अपनी' शब्द 'माँ' की विशेषता बता रहा है, इसलिए यह विशेषण है।

questions.text: Identify the figure of speech in the line: 'The wind stood up and gave a shout.'
questions.explanation: The wind is given human qualities of standing up and shouting, which is personification.

questions.text: Which of the following is a correct example of a transitive verb?
options: C) The cat caught the mouse.
questions.answer: C) The cat caught the mouse.
questions.explanation: A transitive verb requires a direct object, which in this case is 'the mouse'.

questions.text: In the sentence 'The old house looked as if it had been abandoned for years', what is the function of the clause 'as if it had been abandoned for years'?
questions.explanation: This clause modifies the verb 'looked' by describing how the house looked, functioning as an adverb.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a palindrome?
questions.explanation: A palindrome is a word that reads the same backward as forward, like 'level'.

questions.text: Identify the correct form of the verb in the conditional sentence: 'If I _____ you, I would apologize immediately.'
questions.explanation: In the second conditional, we use 'were' for all subjects, even 'I', 'he', 'she', or 'it'.

questions.text: Which literary device is used in the phrase: 'The room was as cold as a tomb'?
questions.explanation: A simile is a comparison between two different things using 'like' or 'as'.

questions.text: Choose the sentence with correct punctuation: 'Please bring the following items a pen paper and your notebook.'
options: A) Please bring the following items: a pen, paper, and your notebook.
B) Please bring the following items, a pen, paper and your notebook.
C) Please bring the following items a pen, paper and your notebook.
D) Please bring the following items: a pen paper and your notebook.
questions.answer: A) Please bring the following items: a pen, paper, and your notebook.
questions.explanation: A colon is used to introduce a list, and commas should separate the items in the list.

questions.text: In the sentence 'The committee has made its decision', what is the antecedent of the pronoun 'its'?
questions.explanation: The antecedent is the noun that the pronoun refers back to, which in this case is 'committee'.

questions.text: Which of the following sentences is in the passive voice?
options: A) The teacher corrected the test papers.
B) The test papers were corrected by the teacher.
C) The teacher is correcting the test papers.
D) The test papers are being corrected by the teacher.
questions.answer: B) The test papers were corrected by the teacher.
questions.explanation: Passive voice occurs when the subject receives the action of the verb, often using 'by'.

questions.text: Identify the type of conjunction in the sentence: 'She wanted to go to the park, but it started raining.'
questions.explanation: But is a coordinating conjunction that connects two independent clauses of equal importance.

questions.text: Identify the figure of speech used in: 'The wind stood up and gave a shout'
questions.explanation: The wind is given human qualities by standing up and shouting, which is a clear example of personification.

questions.text: Choose the correct form of the verb: Neither the teacher nor the students ______ happy with the results.
questions.explanation: When two subjects are joined by 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the subject closer to it, which is 'students' (plural).

questions.text: What is the antonym of 'Eloquent'?
questions.explanation: 'Eloquent' means fluent and persuasive in speaking or writing, so its antonym would be 'inarticulate', meaning unable to express ideas clearly.

questions.text: Identify the type of sentence: 'What a beautiful sunset!'
questions.explanation: The sentence expresses strong emotion and ends with an exclamation mark, making it an exclamatory sentence.

questions.text: Which of the following is a correct transformation of the sentence: 'He said to me, 'I will come tomorrow.''
options: A) He told me that he would come the next day.
B) He told me that he will come the next day.
C) He told me that he would come tomorrow.
D) He told me that he will come tomorrow.
questions.answer: A) He told me that he would come the next day.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, 'said to' changes to 'told', future tense changes to conditional, and 'tomorrow' changes to 'the next day'.

questions.text: Find the word that is correctly spelt:
questions.explanation: 'Necessary' is the correct spelling with one 'c' and two 's's, unlike the other options.

questions.text: Identify the poetic device used in: 'The school bell rang like a trumpet call'
questions.explanation: The comparison uses 'like' to compare the school bell's sound to a trumpet call, which is a simile.

questions.text: Choose the correct preposition: She is afraid ______ spiders.
questions.explanation: The correct preposition to use with 'afraid' is 'of', as in 'afraid of something'.

questions.text: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct?
options: A) Each of the boys have completed their homework.
B) Each of the boys has completed his homework.
C) Each of the boys have completed his homework.
D) Each of the boys has completed their homework.
questions.answer: B) Each of the boys has completed his homework.
questions.explanation: The subject 'each' is singular and requires a singular verb 'has'. When referring to each individually, 'his' is the appropriate pronoun.

questions.text: Identify the type of clause in: 'When the rain stopped, we went out to play'
questions.explanation: The clause 'When the rain stopped' functions as an adverb, modifying the verb 'went' by telling us when the action occurred.

questions.text: Which of the following factors was most responsible for the decline of the textile industry in India during the colonial period?
options: A) Introduction of power looms in Britain
B) High tariffs on Indian imports in Britain
D) Decline in cotton production in India
questions.answer: A) Introduction of power looms in Britain
questions.explanation: The introduction of power looms in Britain made their production faster and cheaper, making it difficult for Indian handloom weavers to compete in both domestic and international markets.

questions.text: Which Indian leader is known for his 'Doctrine of Passive Resistance' and 'Satyagraha'?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi developed the concepts of 'Satyagraha' and 'Doctrine of Passive Resistance' as methods of non-violent struggle against injustice and colonial rule.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental right guaranteed by the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Right to Property was originally a fundamental right but was removed by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978, and is now a legal right under Article 300A.

questions.text: Which of the following rivers is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar'?
questions.explanation: The Kosi river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar' due to its frequent and devastating floods that cause extensive damage to life and property in the region.

questions.text: Which of the following is the main reason for the rapid growth of the service sector in India?
questions.explanation: The growth of the service sector in India has been significantly driven by the development of information technology, IT-enabled services, and business process outsourcing.

questions.text: Which of the following features distinguishes a federal system from a unitary system?
options: B) Division of powers between central and state governments
D) Uniform laws for the entire country
questions.answer: B) Division of powers between central and state governments
questions.explanation: A federal system is characterized by the division of powers between a central government and state governments, whereas in a unitary system, all powers are concentrated in the central government.

questions.text: Which of the following movements was primarily aimed at the abolition of untouchability?
questions.explanation: The Temple Entry Movement, particularly in the princely state of Travancore, was specifically aimed at securing the rights of Dalits to enter Hindu temples, challenging the practice of untouchability.

questions.text: Which of the following is a major environmental consequence of excessive use of chemical fertilizers in agriculture?
questions.explanation: Excessive use of chemical fertilizers leads to nutrient runoff into water bodies, causing eutrophication which depletes oxygen and harms aquatic life.

questions.text: Which of the following was the main objective of the 'Green Revolution' in India?
questions.explanation: The Green Revolution was primarily aimed at increasing agricultural productivity through the introduction of high-yielding variety seeds, chemical fertilizers, and modern farming techniques.

questions.text: Which of the following statements best describes the concept of 'Sarvodaya' as envisioned by Jayaprakash Narayan?
questions.explanation: Sarvodaya, meaning 'welfare of all', was a concept developed by Jayaprakash Narayan based on Gandhi's idea of Antodaya, emphasizing the upliftment of all sections of society, especially the poorest.

questions.text: Malaria is transmitted by the bite of:
questions.explanation: Female Anopheles carries Plasmodium; Aedes spreads dengue and chikungunya.

questions.text: In a DNA double helix, one complete turn covers a distance of about:
questions.explanation: One turn = 10 base pairs × 0.34 nm rise per pair ≈ 3.4 nm; 2 nm is the helix diameter.

questions.text: Which organelle is called the 'suicidal bag' of the cell?
questions.explanation: Lysosomes hold digestive enzymes that can break down the cell itself if the membrane ruptures.

questions.text: The primary CO₂ acceptor in the C4 pathway is:
questions.explanation: Phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP) fixes CO₂ in mesophyll cells forming OAA; RuBP is the C3 acceptor.

questions.text: Which of the following is a dimensionless quantity?
questions.explanation: Strain = change/original (same units cancel), so it has no dimensions; stress and pressure are N/m².

questions.text: Newton's third law explains:
options: A) Why a gun recoils when fired
B) Why planets orbit the sun
C) Why satellites stay in orbit
questions.answer: A) Why a gun recoils when fired
questions.explanation: The bullet's forward momentum produces an equal backward push on the gun — action-reaction pair.

questions.text: A force does zero work on a moving body when the angle between force and displacement is:
questions.explanation: W = Fs cosθ; at θ = 90°, cosθ = 0, so no work is done (e.g. centripetal force in circular motion).

questions.text: The derivative of sin 2x with respect to x is:
questions.explanation: Chain rule: d/dx[sin(2x)] = cos(2x) × d/dx(2x) = 2cos 2x.

questions.text: In how many ways can 4 students be seated in a row of 4 chairs?
questions.explanation: Arrangements = 4! = 4×3×2×1 = 24.

questions.text: The value of sin²30° + cos²30° is:
questions.explanation: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 for every θ — the identity holds regardless of the angle.

questions.text: If A = {1, 2, 3}, how many subsets does A have?
questions.explanation: A set with n elements has 2ⁿ subsets: 2³ = 8 (including ∅ and A itself).

questions.text: Phenol is more acidic than ethanol because:
options: A) It has more carbon atoms
B) The phenoxide ion is resonance stabilised
C) It contains two oxygen atoms
questions.answer: B) The phenoxide ion is resonance stabilised
questions.explanation: The negative charge of phenoxide delocalises into the aromatic ring, stabilising it far more than ethoxide.

questions.text: The coordination number of cobalt in [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]⁺ is:
questions.explanation: Four NH₃ plus two Cl⁻ ligands bind to Co, giving coordination number 6 (octahedral).

questions.text: For a first-order reaction, the half-life is:
options: B) Inversely proportional to rate constant
questions.explanation: t½ = 0.693/k for first order — a defining feature; zero-order half-life does depend on concentration.

questions.text: Which concentration term does NOT change with temperature?
questions.explanation: Molality uses mass of solvent (mass is temperature-independent); the others involve volume, which expands on heating.

questions.text: For a spontaneous cell reaction, which must be true?
questions.explanation: Spontaneity needs ΔG° = −nFE°cell < 0, which requires E°cell > 0 and hence log K > 0.

questions.text: In a pure inductive AC circuit, current:
questions.explanation: For an inductor, current lags the applied voltage by 90°; in a capacitor it leads by 90°.

questions.text: Power of a convex lens of focal length 25 cm is:
questions.explanation: P = 1/f(in metres) = 1/0.25 = +4 dioptre; convex lenses have positive power.

questions.text: A charged particle enters a magnetic field parallel to B. Its path will be:
questions.explanation: Magnetic force qv × B is zero when v is parallel to B, so the particle continues undeflected.

questions.text: Drift velocity of electrons in a conductor is of the order of:
questions.explanation: Despite the huge random thermal speeds, the slow net drift is around fractions of a mm/s, i.e. ~10⁻⁴ m/s.

questions.text: The electric field inside a uniformly charged conducting spherical shell is:
questions.explanation: Charges reside on the surface; by Gauss's law no flux is enclosed by an interior surface, so E = 0 inside.

questions.text: Which tissue transports water and minerals upward in plants?
questions.explanation: Xylem carries water and minerals from roots upward; phloem transports food both ways.

questions.text: Sound waves in air are:
questions.explanation: Air particles vibrate along the direction of propagation, and a material medium is required — longitudinal mechanical wave.

questions.text: The number of molecules in 2 moles of CO₂ is approximately:
questions.explanation: 1 mole has 6.022 × 10²³ molecules, so 2 moles have 1.2044 × 10²⁴.

questions.text: If the distance between two masses is doubled, the gravitational force between them becomes:
questions.explanation: Force ∝ 1/r²; doubling r multiplies force by 1/4.

questions.text: A car accelerates uniformly from rest to 20 m/s in 8 s. Its acceleration is:
The mean of first five prime numbers is:
In triangles ABC and PQR, AB = QR, BC = PR and CA = PQ. Then:
questions.explanation: Match corresponding equal sides: A↔Q, B↔R, C↔P, so △ABC ≅ △QRP by SSS.

questions.text: The graph of x = −3 is a line:
questions.explanation: x = constant fixes the x-coordinate everywhere, giving a vertical line parallel to the y-axis, 3 units left of origin.

questions.text: If p(x) = x³ − 3x² + 2, then p(1) equals:
questions.explanation: p(1) = 1 − 3 + 2 = 0, so (x − 1) is a factor.

questions.text: Which of the following is an irrational number?
questions.explanation: The pattern is non-terminating and non-repeating, hence irrational. 0.252525… repeats, √16 = 4, and (22/7)÷(22/7) = 1.

questions.text: Which structure increases the absorptive surface of the human small intestine?
questions.explanation: Villi are finger-like folds of the intestinal lining that absorb digested food; alveoli belong to lungs, nephrons to kidneys.

questions.text: Two 6 Ω resistors are connected in parallel and the combination in series with a 3 Ω resistor. Total resistance is:
questions.explanation: Parallel pair: 3 Ω. In series with 3 Ω: 3 + 3 = 6 Ω.

questions.text: An object placed at the principal focus of a concave mirror forms an image that is:
options: A) Virtual and erect at focus
B) Real, inverted and highly diminished at focus
C) Real, inverted and highly enlarged at infinity
D) Same size at centre of curvature
questions.answer: C) Real, inverted and highly enlarged at infinity
questions.explanation: When the object is at F, reflected rays become parallel, so the image forms at infinity, real, inverted and highly enlarged.

questions.text: A solution turns phenolphthalein pink. Its pH is most likely:

questions.text: Respiration in living cells is an example of which type of reaction?
questions.explanation: Glucose is oxidised to CO₂ and water, releasing energy as heat — exothermic oxidation.

questions.text: For x² − 6x + k = 0 to have two equal real roots, k must equal:
